# Overview

The objective of this work is to create a decision model to augment adjunctive vasopressor selection in adults with septic shock. Patient encounters meeting clinical criteria for septic shock, whether Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Adult Sepsis Event (CDC ASE) or Third International Consensus Definition for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3) criteria, were previously identified. We will first divide the cohort of patients with septic shock from the Cleveland Clinic Ohio region into sub-cohorts based on second-line adjunctive vasopressor received (such as vasopressin or epinephrine). Using these sub-cohorts, we will create and calibrate separate treatment-specific clinical prediction models for adjunctive vasopressor response, defined as achievement of a mean arterial pressure (MAP) ≥65 mm Hg and a decrease in norepinephrine-equivalent vasopressor dose at six hours after adjunct response. The models will be derived using candidate predictors of patient characteristics, treatment context factors, and shock characteristics measured at first adjunctive vasopressor initiation. We will build and optimize prediction models within each sub-cohort with regression-based and machine learning algorithms for binary categorical outcomes. The prediction model with the best performance (based on predictive discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and implementation readiness) in each sub-cohort will be considered the final model and carried forward.

We will then define for each patient the decision model-recommended adjunctive vasopressor based on the medication with the highest predicted likelihood of response for a given patient. To validate the model, we will conduct a discordance analysis using patients with septic shock from the Cleveland Clinic Florida region. For each patient, the model-recommended second-line adjunctive vasopressor therapy will be compared against the observed decision made in the standard process of care. Concordance will be defined as a patient given the second-line adjunctive vasopressor consistent with the decision model recommendation. Discordance will be defined as a patient given an adjunctive vasopressor differing from the medication recommended by the decision model. Each patient will be defined as receiving concordant or discordant therapy, creating counterfactual controls for model recommendations. The global effect of discordance will be defined as the odds ratio (estimated with logistic regression) for adjunctive vasopressor response comparing discordant decisions to concordant decisions.

# Load Data

See [Bauer 2025](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13054-025-05749-1) and open source Quarto documents for development of [the patient cohort](https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/sepsis-case-identification-workflow) and an [initial norepinephrine failure prediction model](https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/septic_shock_ne_failure_model), which contain the process steps to build the patient cohorts and .Rds files. # Data Creation

Next, select vectors already in the tibble that will be used for modeling. Then identify and create vectors for exposure risk, covariates, and outcomes that will be used for modeling.

## Select Vectors {#sec-transform}

Create a new tibble (`adj`) filtered to patients in the `ne_incl` tibble who received an adjunctive vasopressor. In the same call, select out columns (vectors) that will not be used for joining data between tibbles or for modeling, change the column ordering, rename one column, drop unused factor levels, and adjust the levels for some categorical variables.

```{r}
adj <- ne_incl |>
  filter(event_3_level_type == "1-adjunct") |>
  select(-c(event, event_type, surv_hours, any_adj, surv_obj, 
            surv_hours_3_level, hours_to_death, wt_time, wt_kg, prior_abx,
            mv_before_shock, surg_service_30d_prior_to_dc, prior_surg_service, 
            shock_onset_minus_6h, shock_onset_minus_12h, shock_onset_minus_24h, 
            event_3_level, event_3_level_type
            )
         ) |>
  rename(sepsis_onset_tot_sofa = tot_sofa) |>
  droplevels() |>
  mutate(criteria_met = fct_relevel(criteria_met, "Both", "ASE only"),
         race_eth = fct_recode(race_eth,
                               "Other, non-Hispanic" = "Asian",
                               "Black, non-Hispanic" = "Black",
                               "Hispanic or Latino" = "Hispanic or Latino",
                               "Multiracial, non-Hispanic" = "Multiracial",
                               "Other, non-Hispanic" = "Other",
                               "White, non-Hispanic" = "White"),
         race_eth = fct_relevel(race_eth, 
                               "Black, non-Hispanic", 
                               "Hispanic or Latino",
                               "Multiracial, non-Hispanic",
                               "Other, non-Hispanic",
                               "White, non-Hispanic"
                               ),
         shock_onset_hosp_beds_cat = 
           fct_relevel(shock_onset_hosp_beds_cat, "≥500", "200-499"),
         shock_onset_hosp_teaching_status = 
           fct_relevel(shock_onset_hosp_teaching_status, "Non-teaching"),
         shock_onset_tx_unit = 
           fct_relevel(shock_onset_tx_unit, "Medical/Cardiac ICU"),
         ssc_era = fct_relevel(ssc_era, "SSC 2021")
         )
```

Now check the vector names in the `adj` tibble to confirm expectations are met.

```{r}
names(adj)
```

The retained columns (vectors) are consistent with expectations.

## Outcome: Adjunctive Vasopressor Response {#sec-out}

The outcome of interest will be adjunctive vasopressor blood pressure response, defined as achieving MAP ≥65 mm Hg with a decrease from baseline in norepinephrine dosage at 6 hours after first adjunctive vasopressor initiation.

-   The outcome will only be adjudicated for the first adjunctive agent (the "second-line" vasopressor).

-   Patients with an unavailable (missing) MAP value at 6 hours (or within the 3 hours preceding \[missing MAP in hours 3-6 after adjunct start\]) will be adjudicated as not meeting response criteria. The impact of this component of the criteria will be explored.

-   Because additional ("third-line", etc.) adjunctive vasopressors may be initiated within the 6 hour window period, the norepinephrine-equivalent (NEQ) dose at 6 hours will be utilized instead of solely the norepinephrine dose. The NEQ will be based on the Kotani equivalence equation ([Kotani 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36670410/)).

The outcome adjudication will be operationalized as follows.

1.  Join closest MAP (and within 3 hours) to the `pressors_doses` tibble for each dose titration. This value will be used for the adjudication of the MAP value at 6 hours after adjunct start. Joining the MAP in this way will have two added advantages: a) availability of closest MAP at adjunct start (which will be identified in a subsequent section for use as a predictor), and b) allow for calculation of the ratio of MAP to norepinephrine-equivalent dose (MAP/NEQ) for each dose, which will be added at the end of the call for potential future use.

```{r}
pressors_doses <- pressors_doses |>
  mutate(mar_taken_minus_3h = mar_taken_time - dhours(3)) |>
  left_join(map |> 
              # Filter MAP values to plausible range for patient in shock
              filter(map >=15 & map <=120) |>
              select(encounter_id, map_time, map) |>
              # Arrange to have the higher MAP from invasive and non-invasive
              # devices that were taken at the exact same time
              arrange(encounter_id, map_time, desc(map)) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, map_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(mar_taken_time >= map_time),
                         mar_taken_minus_3h <= map_time
                         ),
            relationship = "many-to-one"
            ) |>
  rename(closest_map_time = map_time,
         closest_map = map) |>
  mutate(map_neq_goradia = if_else(running_nee_kotani != 0 & 
                                     !is.na(closest_map),
                                   closest_map / running_nee_goradia,
                                   NA
                                   ),
         map_neq_kotani = if_else(running_nee_kotani != 0 & 
                                     !is.na(closest_map),
                                  closest_map / running_nee_kotani,
                                  NA
                                  )
         )

# Remove `map` tibble since it won't be used moving forward
rm(map)
```

2.  Determine the date/time of the first adjunctive vasopressor start (`first_adj_time`) in the `pressors_courses` tibble and join this vector to the `adj` tibble.

```{r}
pressors_courses <- pressors_courses |>
  mutate(first_adj_time = as.POSIXct(case_when(
    first_adj == "vasopressin" ~ vasopressin_start,
    first_adj == "epinephrine" ~ epinephrine_start,
    first_adj == "phenylephrine" ~ phenylephrine_start,
    first_adj == "dopamine" ~ dopamine_start,
    first_adj == "AVP + Epi" ~ vasopressin_start,
    first_adj == "AVP + PE" ~ vasopressin_start,
    first_adj == "Epi + PE" ~ epinephrine_start,
    first_adj == "AVP + DA" ~ vasopressin_start,
    first_adj == "AVP + Epi + PE" ~ vasopressin_start,
    first_adj == "Epi + DA" ~ epinephrine_start,
    is.na(first_adj) ~ NA,
    # Create "error" date/time to ensure all options captured in coding
    .default = as.POSIXct(1900-01-01)
    )))
```

Ensure coding didn't result in any error date/time

```{r}
sum(pressors_courses$first_adj_time == as.POSIXct(1900-01-01), na.rm = TRUE)
```

No error resulted, therefore continue with the join.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  left_join(pressors_courses |> select(encounter_id, first_adj_time),
            by = join_by(encounter_id),
            relationship = "one-to-one"
            ) |>
  relocate(c(first_adj_time, first_adj, hours_to_first_adj), 
           .after = encounter_id
           )
```

3.  To the `adj` tibble, join from the `pressors_doses` tibble the closest NEQ dose before the time of first adjunct start (but not before or equal to the time of first adjunct start because the NEQ at the time equal to the first adjunct start includes the initial adjunct dose). While this baseline value only includes the norepinephrine dosage, this will be called `adj_baseline_neq` for clarity. Also join the NEQ with units of mcg/min and the MAP/NEQ for completeness. These values will not be used other than for description of the cohort of included patients.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  left_join(pressors_doses |> 
              select(encounter_id, mar_taken_time, running_nee_kotani,
                     running_nee_kotani_mcg_min, map_neq_kotani
                     ) |>
              distinct(),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time > mar_taken_time)
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one"
            ) |>
  select(-mar_taken_time) |>
  rename(adj_baseline_neq = running_nee_kotani,
         adj_baseline_neq_mcg_min = running_nee_kotani_mcg_min,
         adj_baseline_map_neq = map_neq_kotani) |>
  relocate(adj_baseline_neq, .after = hours_to_first_adj)
```

Confirm no missing values for `adj_baseline_neq`.

```{r}
sum(is.na(adj$adj_baseline_neq))
```

There are no missing values. 

Review random sample of all cases to ensure expectations met (commented out for rendering).

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
df <- adj |> 
  select(encounter_id, first_adj, first_adj_time, adj_baseline_neq) |>
  slice_sample(n=10)
#View(df |> arrange(encounter_id))
#View(pressors_doses |> filter(encounter_id %in% df$encounter_id) |>
#       select(encounter_id, mar_taken_time, medication, titrate_action, 
#              running_nee_kotani
#              ) |>
#       arrange(encounter_id)
#     )
rm(df)
```

Expectations are met, therefore continue.

Assess if any values of `adj_baseline_neq` are zero (doses must be greater than zero to indicate adjunctive vasopressor use). 

```{r}
sum(adj$adj_baseline_neq == 0)
```

There are 369 cases where the norepinephrine dosage documented immediately before adjunct initiation was zero. Review some of these cases to determine if there is an issue with the joining process or if they indicate true cessations of norepinephrine (commented out for rendering purposes).

```{r}
df <- adj |> filter(adj_baseline_neq == 0) |> head(n=10)
#View(df)
#View(pressors_doses |> filter(encounter_id %in% df$encounter_id))
rm(df)
```

In the manual review most norepinephrine doses were truly documented as zero immediately prior to first "adjunct" vasopressor initiation. These cases should be subsequently excluded because they do not represent adjunctive vasopressor usage: the start of the non-norepinephrine vasopressor represents monotherapy with that medication. 

There was one case, though, in the manual review that had a norepinephrine dosage of zero immediately preceding the adjunct start but at the same time of adjunct start there was a non-zero norepinephrine dosage documented. To account for these cases join the norepinephrine dosage at the exact time of first adjunct start, then replace the `adj_baseline_neq` dose of zero with the norepinephrine dosage at the exact time of first adjunct start. Also join `adj_baseline_neq_mcg_min` and calculate `adj_baseline_map_neq` for these cases with the alternative join criteria.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  left_join(pressors_doses |> 
              filter(medication == "norepinephrine") |>
              select(encounter_id, mar_taken_time, nee_kotani, closest_map,
                     dose_mcg_min) |>
              distinct(),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         first_adj_time == mar_taken_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one"
            ) |>
  mutate(adj_baseline_neq = if_else(adj_baseline_neq == 0 & !is.na(nee_kotani),
                                    nee_kotani,
                                    adj_baseline_neq
                                    ),
         adj_baseline_neq_mcg_min = if_else(adj_baseline_neq == 0 & 
                                              !is.na(dose_mcg_min) &
                                              dose_mcg_min != 0,
                                    dose_mcg_min,
                                    adj_baseline_neq_mcg_min
                                    ),
         adj_baseline_map_neq = if_else(is.na(adj_baseline_map_neq) & 
                                          !is.na(nee_kotani) & 
                                          nee_kotani != 0 &
                                          !is.na(closest_map),
                                        closest_map / nee_kotani,
                                        adj_baseline_map_neq
                                        )
         ) |>
  select(-c(nee_kotani, closest_map))

sum(adj$adj_baseline_neq == 0)
sum(adj$adj_baseline_neq_mcg_min == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
nrow(adj |> filter(is.na(adj_baseline_map_neq)))

```

4.  To the `adj` tibble, join from the `pressors_doses` tibble the NEQ and MAP values from the time closest to 6 hours after first adjunct start (and also equal to or after initiation of the first adjunct). Also join the MAP/NEQ for completeness. Only joining values after initiation of the first adjunct (not equal to) was considered, but since an adjunct contributes to the NEQ, if there are no subsequent NEQ values documented then non-response should be adjudicated.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj |> 
              mutate(first_adj_plus_6h = first_adj_time + dhours(6)),
            pressors_doses |> 
              select(encounter_id, mar_taken_time, 
                     running_nee_kotani, closest_map, map_neq_kotani
                     ) |>
              distinct(),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_plus_6h >= mar_taken_time),
                         first_adj_time <= mar_taken_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one"
            ) |>
  select(-mar_taken_time) |>
  rename(adj_plus6h_neq = running_nee_kotani,
         adj_plus6h_map = closest_map,
         adj_plus6h_map_neq = map_neq_kotani
         ) |>
  relocate(c(adj_plus6h_neq, adj_plus6h_map), .after = adj_baseline_neq)
```

Check for missing values from the join.

```{r}
sum(is.na(adj$adj_plus6h_neq))
paste0(round_half_up((sum(is.na(adj$adj_plus6h_neq))/nrow(adj))*100,0),"%")
sum(is.na(adj$adj_plus6h_map))
paste0(round_half_up((sum(is.na(adj$adj_plus6h_map))/nrow(adj))*100,0),"%")
```

There are no missing values for the NEQ and 282 (3%) observations have a missing value for MAP at 6 hours after first adjunct start. This will be evaluated as part of the adjunctive vasopressor response criteria.

5.  Lastly, determine first adjunctive vasopressor response criteria as being met if MAP ≥65 mm hg at 6 hours after first adjunct start (`adj_plus6h_map`) **and** NEQ at 6 hours after first adjunct start (`adj_plus6h_neq`) is \< baseline NEQ (`adj_baseline_neq`).
    -   If `death_time` prior to baseline time plus 6 hours then adjudicate as not meeting criteria (death before 6 hours == non-response)
    -   If NEQ at 6 hours is the same or higher than baseline NEQ then adjudicate as not meeting criteria. Notably, initiation of additional adjunctive vasopressors (third-line, etc.) between first adjunct start and 6 hours after first adjunct start are accounted for through the contribution of their doses to the NEQ component.
    -   If MAP \<65 mm Hg at 6 hours then adjudicate as not meeting criteria
    -   If NEQ or MAP at 6 hours is missing then adjudicate as not meeting criteria (no evidence of lower NEQ or MAP at goal)
    -   Response criteria met if MAP ≥65 mm Hg at 6 hours *and* NEQ at 6 hours is lower than baseline NEQ

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  mutate(
    response_type = factor(case_when(
      !is.na(death_time) & death_time <= first_adj_plus_6h ~ "0-no_resp_death",
      adj_plus6h_neq >= adj_baseline_neq ~ "0-no_resp_neq_same_or_higher",
      adj_plus6h_map < 65 ~ "0-no_resp_map_below_65", 
      is.na(adj_plus6h_neq) ~ "2-resp_unclear_neq_missing",
      is.na(adj_plus6h_map) ~ "2-resp_unclear_map_missing",
      adj_plus6h_map >= 65 & adj_plus6h_neq < adj_baseline_neq ~ "1-response",
      .default = "Error"), 
      levels = c("1-response", "0-no_resp_neq_same_or_higher", 
                 "0-no_resp_map_below_65", "0-no_resp_death",
                 "2-resp_unclear_neq_missing", "2-resp_unclear_map_missing"
                 )
      ),
    response = factor(if_else(response_type == "1-response",
                              "Response",
                              "No Response"),
                      # Ensure level ordering is correct for modeling
                      levels = c("No Response", "Response")
      )
    )
```

Show levels of `response_type`, which also serves as a check to ensure all scenarios are accounted for (no "Error" appears).

```{r}
adj |> tabyl(response_type) |> adorn_totals() |> adorn_pct_formatting()
```

First, no "Error" appears, therefore the code worked as intended.

Second, the incidence of response (32%) is lower than in our previous work with vasopressin alone (40%) but is reasonably close. The difference is explainable because patients and criteria in the previous work were slightly different - in this work all patients received initial norepinephrine (previously all initial vasopressors were included), death between first adjunct start and 6 hours later was considered non-response (not considered in prior work), the vasopressor contribution of vasopressin (equated through the Kotani norepinephrine-equivalent dose \[NEQ\]) was considered in the response criteria (previously it was ignored), and the NEQ was required to be lower than baseline (not lower or equal to baseline since the vasopressin NEQ contribution was considered). Inclusion of the vasopressor contribution of vasopressin as part of the NEQ is likely the largest driver of the difference in response incidence between studies.

Third, only 58 observations (0.7%) were adjudicated as not meeting response criteria because a MAP value in the 3 to 6 hour period after first adjunct start was unavailable. If the alternative approach where missing MAP values are ignored (considered as meeting response because no evidence MAP was below goal) were to be utilized then the frequency of response would not change in a meaningful way (\<1% difference). Therefore, will continue with the approach of considering missing MAP values as criteria not being met.

## Patient Descriptors and Candidate Predictors

This sub-section will create and join case eligibility criteria and patient characteristics, some of which are candidate predictors of interest.

### Biological and Context Characteristics

Some of the covariates (predictors) of interest are in the `adj` tibble already, but some additional covariates of interest need to be joined from other loaded tibbles.

#### Body Weight

Join body weight at first adjunct start from the `body_weight` tibble.

```{r}
adj <- left_join(
  adj,
  body_weight |> select(encounter_id, wt_time, wt_kg) |> distinct(),
  by = join_by(encounter_id,
               closest(first_adj_time >= wt_time)
               ),
  relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  select(-wt_time) |>
  rename(first_adj_wt_kg = wt_kg)

# Remove `body_weight` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(body_weight)
```

#### Treatment Unit

Join treatment unit (department), service, and ICU type (if applicable) at first adjunct start based on admission/discharge/transfer (ADT) data in the `adt` tibble.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  left_join(adt |> select(encounter_id, in_effective_time, out_effective_time,
                first_adj_hospital = hospital,
                first_adj_department_name = department_name, 
                first_adj_hospital_service = hospital_service, 
                first_adj_icu_group = icu_group, 
                first_adj_unit_type = unit_type),
            join_by(encounter_id,
                    closest(first_adj_time >= in_effective_time),
                    first_adj_time <= out_effective_time),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
            mutate(first_adj_unit_type = fct_relevel(first_adj_unit_type,
                                                     "ED", "Ward", "ICU")) |>
  select(-in_effective_time, -out_effective_time)
```

There are some observations with first adjunct start time occurring between unit-specific admission and discharge times in the `adt` tibble due to inconsistency in manual time stamps or back-dated documentation during transport between units. This results in some observations having NA for the characteristics because the join criteria are not met. The call below counts the number of observations having NA for the `first_adj_hospital` vector (as a representative example).

```{r}
sum(is.na(adj$first_adj_hospital))
```

There are 10 observations (patients) with missing `first_adj_hospital`. The call below replaces these NA values with the characteristics from the treatment unit preceding the `first_adj_time`.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  left_join(adt |> 
              select(encounter_id, in_effective_time, out_effective_time,
                hospital, department_name, hospital_service, icu_group, 
                unit_type),
            join_by(encounter_id,
                    closest(first_adj_time > out_effective_time)),
            relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  arrange(encounter_id, first_adj_time, desc(out_effective_time)) |>
  distinct(encounter_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(first_adj_hospital = 
           coalesce(first_adj_hospital, hospital),
         first_adj_department_name = 
           coalesce(first_adj_department_name, department_name),
         first_adj_hospital_service = 
           coalesce(first_adj_hospital_service, hospital_service),
         first_adj_icu_group = coalesce(first_adj_icu_group, icu_group),
         first_adj_unit_type = coalesce(first_adj_unit_type, unit_type)) |>
  select(-c(in_effective_time, out_effective_time, hospital, department_name, 
            hospital_service, icu_group, unit_type))

# Remove `adt` tibble since it won't be used moving forward
rm(adt)
```

Join hospital characteristics.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  left_join(hosp_char |> select(hospital, hosp_beds_cat, hosp_teaching_status,
                                hosp_state),
            by = join_by(first_adj_hospital == hospital),
            relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) |>
  rename(first_adj_hosp_beds_cat = hosp_beds_cat,
         first_adj_hosp_teaching_status = hosp_teaching_status,
         first_adj_hosp_state = hosp_state
  ) |>
  relocate(c(first_adj_hosp_beds_cat, first_adj_hosp_teaching_status,
             first_adj_hosp_state
             ),
           .after = first_adj_hospital)

# Remove `hosp_char` tibble since it won't be used moving forward
rm(hosp_char)
```

The `adj` tibble now has a vector for the treatment location at the time of first adjunct start (`first_adj_unit_type`) but this is too broad of a categorization. Contrastingly, the `first_adj_icu_group` vector for ICU designations is too granular for external applicability. Therefore a new vector (`first_adj_tx_unit`) will be created that combines information from these vectors to generate categories.

```{r}
adj <- adj |> mutate(first_adj_tx_unit = factor(case_when(
  first_adj_unit_type == "ED" | first_adj_unit_type == "Ward" ~ "ED/Rapid Response",
  first_adj_unit_type == "ICU" &
    grepl("MICU", first_adj_icu_group) ~ "Medical ICU",
  first_adj_unit_type == "ICU" &
    grepl("CCU", first_adj_icu_group) ~ "Cardiac ICU",
  first_adj_unit_type == "ICU" &
    grepl("SICU|CVICU", first_adj_icu_group) ~ "Surgical ICU",
  first_adj_unit_type == "ICU" ~ "Mixed Med/Surg ICU",
  .default = NA
  )))
```

Now show the distribution of values to ensure expectations are met.

```{r}
adj |> tabyl(first_adj_tx_unit) |> adorn_pct_formatting() |> 
  adorn_totals() |> 
  rename("First Adjunct Start Treatment Unit" = "first_adj_tx_unit") |>
  kable(align = c('lcc')) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

### Adjunct Start Characteristics

Transform variables at the time of first adjunctive vasopressor start (baseline).

#### Antimicrobials

Antimicrobial administration within the 24 hours prior to first adjunct start. This will be adjudicated based on the `abx_range_start` and `abx_range_end` variables in the `abx` tibble. Antibiotic start must be prior to first adjunct start and the last dose of antibiotics as part of the course must be given within 24 hours prior to first adjunct start. This will account for antibiotic courses that are "ongoing" at first adjunct start.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(
    adj |> mutate(first_adj_minus_24h = first_adj_time - dhours(24)),
    abx |> select(encounter_id, abx_range_start, abx_range_end),
    join_by(encounter_id,
            closest(first_adj_time >= abx_range_start),
            first_adj_minus_24h <= abx_range_end),
    relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  distinct(encounter_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(first_adj_abx = factor(if_else(!is.na(abx_range_start),
                                     "Antibiotics", "No Antibiotics"
                                     ))) |>
  arrange(encounter_id, admission_time) |>
  select(-c(abx_range_start, abx_range_end, first_adj_minus_24h))

# Remove `abx` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(abx) 
```

#### Surgery

First, join the `patient_id` identifier from the `encounter_key` tibble to the `adj` tibble.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  left_join(encounter_key |> select(episode_key, patient_id),
            join_by(encounter_id == episode_key),
            relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  distinct(encounter_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

Next adjudicate surgery within the 30 days prior to adjunct start.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(
    adj |> mutate(first_adj_minus_30d = first_adj_time - ddays(30)),
    surg |> select(patient_id, surgery_start_time),
    join_by(patient_id,
            first_adj_minus_30d <= surgery_start_time,
            first_adj_time >= surgery_start_time),
    relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  arrange(encounter_id, surgery_start_time) |>
  distinct(encounter_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(prior_surg = factor(if_else(!is.na(surgery_start_time),
                                     "Surgery", "No Surgery"
                                     ))) |>
  arrange(encounter_id, admission_time) |>
  select(-surgery_start_time, -first_adj_minus_30d)
# Remove tibbles that won't be used moving forward
rm(surg, encounter_key) 
```

#### Acute Kidney Injury

Acute kidney injury (AKI) will be defined and staged per the [KDIGO 2012 criteria](https://kdigo.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/KDIGO-2012-AKI-Guideline-English.pdf). The urine output component will be omitted due to the lack of reliable data collection in hospitalized patients [Alrawashdeh 2024](https://journals.lww.com/ccmjournal/abstract/2024/09000/the_impact_of_common_variations_in_sequential.6.aspx).

AKI will be staged as follows:

-   Stage 1: Serum creatinine (SCr) 1.5-1.9 times baseline OR ≥0.3 mg/dL increase from baseline
-   Stage 2: SCr 2.0-2.9 times baseline
-   Stage 3: SCr ≥3.0 times baseline OR increase in SCr to ≥4.0 mg/dL OR (new) initiation of renal replacement therapy

Baseline SCr will be determined as follows ([Hoste 2015](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/S00134-015-3934-7), [Alfieri 2023](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0287398)):

-   Median pre-morbid value from the 3 months prior to encounter/admission
-   If pre-morbid SCr not available, minimum value during the encounter observed prior to first adjunct start

Patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) or renal replacement therapy prior to admission will be adjudicated as **not** meeting criteria for Stage 3 AKI.

Retain only SCr values obtained prior to first adjunct start. Then determined baseline SCr value based on criteria above. The work to determine pre-morbid SCr value (`pta_scr`) in the `scr` tibble was done in the `kidney_function.qmd` Quarto document.

```{r}
scr <- 
  left_join(scr,
            adj |> select(encounter_id, first_adj_time),
            by = join_by(encounter_id),
            relationship = "many-to-one"
            ) |>
  mutate(scr_before_adj = 
           if_else(scr_taken_time <= first_adj_time, "Yes", "No")
         ) |>
  filter(scr_before_adj == "Yes") |>
  select(-scr_before_adj) |>
  group_by(encounter_id) |>
  mutate(min_scr_before_adj = min(scr_result)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(baseline_scr = case_when(
    !is.na(pta_scr) ~ pta_scr,
    !is.na(min_scr_before_adj) ~ min_scr_before_adj,
    .default = NA
    ))
```

Join pertinent values from `scr` to `adj` tibble (notably, only join the closest SCr value obtained before first adjunct start).

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj,
            scr |> select(encounter_id, scr_taken_time, scr_result,
                          baseline_scr
                          ) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, scr_taken_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= scr_taken_time)),
            relationship = "one-to-one"
            )
rm(scr) # Remove `scr` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
```

Determine renal replacement therapy (RRT) before first adjunct start. The work to determine new RRT (`new_rrt`) in the `rrt` tibble was done in the `kidney_function.qmd` Quarto document.

```{r}
rrt_before_adj <- 
  left_join(rrt,
            adj |> select(encounter_id, first_adj_time),
            by = join_by(encounter_id),
            relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  mutate(rrt_before_adj = 
           if_else(rrt_taken_time <= first_adj_time, "Yes", "No")
         ) |>
  filter(rrt_before_adj == "Yes") |>
  select(-c(rrt_before_adj))

rrt_before_adj_new <- rrt_before_adj |>
  filter(new_rrt == "Yes")
```

Create variables for RRT before adjunct (`rrt_before_adj`) and new RRT before adjunct (`new_rrt_before_adj`) within the `adj` tibble.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  mutate(rrt_before_adj = factor(
           if_else(encounter_id %in% rrt_before_adj$encounter_id,
                   "RRT Before Adjunct", "No RRT Before Adjunct"
                   )),
         new_rrt_before_adj = 
           if_else(encounter_id %in% rrt_before_adj_new$encounter_id,
                   "Yes", "No"
                   )
         )
# Remove `rrt_before_adj`, `new_rrt_before_adj`, and `rrt` tibbles because  
# they won't be used moving forward
rm(rrt_before_adj, rrt_before_adj_new, rrt)  
```

Now that all necessary variables are available, determine AKI presence and stage in the `adj` tibble. Data for administrative coding for ESKD was managed in the `kidney.qmd` Quarto document.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  mutate(aki = factor(case_when(
    encounter_id %in% esrd$encounter_id ~ "ESKD",
    scr_result / baseline_scr >= 3 |
      scr_result >=4 |
      new_rrt_before_adj == "Yes" ~ "AKI Stage 3",
    (scr_result / baseline_scr >= 2) & 
      (scr_result / baseline_scr < 3) ~ "AKI Stage 2",
    (scr_result / baseline_scr >= 1.5) & 
      (scr_result / baseline_scr < 2) |
      scr_result - baseline_scr >= 0.3 ~ "AKI Stage 1",
    is.na(scr_result) ~ NA,
    .default = "No AKI"
     ))) |>
  mutate(aki = fct_relevel(aki, "No AKI")) |>
  rename(first_adj_aki = aki)
rm(esrd) # Remove `esrd` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
```

Show table of AKI staging. NA values are expected due to instances when an SCr value (`src_result`) is not available before first adjunct start.

```{r}
adj |> tabyl(first_adj_aki) |>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |> 
  adorn_totals() |> 
  rename("Acute Kidney Injury Stage" = "first_adj_aki") |>
  kable(align = c('lcc')) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

The code worked as intended and the counts align with expectations.

Retain only SCr values collected within 24 hours of first adjunct start (SCr values collected before first adjunct start were ensured in an above step).

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  mutate(first_adj_minus_24h = first_adj_time - dhours(24),
         first_adj_scr = 
           if_else(scr_taken_time >= first_adj_minus_24h, scr_result, NA)
         ) |>
  # Remove variables that won't be used moving forward
  select(-c(scr_taken_time, scr_result, baseline_scr, new_rrt_before_adj))
```

#### SOFA-2 Components and Calculation

In this section join components of and calculate the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)-2 score [Ranzani, JAMA 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41159833/). The SOFA-2 includes six organ systems each scored from 0 to 4 points, with a total score ranging from 0 to 24 (higher scores indicate worse organ dysfunction).

##### Brain

The Brain score centers on the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score but includes a clause "For sedated patients, use the last recorded GCS before sedation. If the previous GCS is unknown, score 0". Therefore sedative medication medication administration must be considered when joining the GCS value.

Join sedative medication administration (from the `sed` tibble) within the preceding 6 hours of the GCS value to the `gcs` tibble. Sedatives included in the `sed` tibble are dexmedetomidine, diazepam, fentanyl, hydromorphone, ketamine, lorazepam, midazolam, and propofol administered via any non-epidural route. The 6 hours duration preceding the GCS value was based on an approximation of the duration of these medications (recognizing some medications have a shorter duration).

```{r}
gcs <- left_join(gcs |>
                  select(encounter_id, gcs_taken_time, gcs) |>
                  arrange(encounter_id, gcs_taken_time, gcs) |>
                  distinct(encounter_id, gcs_taken_time, .keep_all = TRUE) |> 
                  mutate(gcs_minus_6h = gcs_taken_time - dhours(6)),
                sed |> select(encounter_id, sed_taken_time = mar_taken_time),
                by = join_by(encounter_id,
                             closest(gcs_taken_time >= sed_taken_time),
                             gcs_minus_6h <= sed_taken_time
                             ),
                relationship = "many-to-many"
                ) |>
  mutate(sed_prev_6h = if_else(!is.na(sed_taken_time), 1, 0)) |>
  arrange(encounter_id, gcs_taken_time, desc(sed_prev_6h)) |>
  distinct(encounter_id, gcs_taken_time, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

Join the closest GCS value from the `gcs` tibble that was obtained without a sedative medication administered in the preceding 6 hours, restricted to values obtained within 6 hours prior to first adjunct start.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj |> 
              mutate(first_adj_minus_6h = first_adj_time - dhours(6)),
            gcs |>
              filter(sed_prev_6h == 0) |>
              select(encounter_id, gcs_taken_time, gcs),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= gcs_taken_time),
                         first_adj_minus_6h <= gcs_taken_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  rename(first_adj_gcs_no_sed = gcs) |>
  # Remove variable that won't be used moving forward
  select(-c(gcs_taken_time))
```

The Brain score also includes a clause "If receiving drug treatment for delirium (short- or long-term), score 1 point even if GCS is 15". Therefore, join delirium medication administration within the preceding 12 hours. The `antipsy` tibble includes the anti-psychotic medications aripiprazole, haloperidol, quetiapine, and ziprasidone, which may be used at the development site for treatment of delirium. Also join dexmedetomidine administration within the preceding 12 hours since it may be used for treatment of delirium as outlined in the 2025 Focused Update to the Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Prevention and Management of Pain, Anxiety, Agitation/Sedation, Delirium, Immobility, and Sleep Disruption in Adult Patients in the ICU [Lewis, Crit Care Med 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39982143/).

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj |>
              mutate(first_adj_minus_12h = first_adj_time - dhours(12)),
            antipsy |> 
              select(encounter_id, antipsy_taken_time = mar_taken_time) |> 
              distinct(),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= antipsy_taken_time),
                         first_adj_minus_12h <= antipsy_taken_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  left_join(sed |> 
              filter(short_name == "dexmedetomidine") |>
              select(encounter_id, dex_taken_time = mar_taken_time) |> 
              distinct(),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= dex_taken_time),
                         first_adj_minus_12h <= dex_taken_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one"
            ) |>
  mutate(delirium_med_prev_12h = 
           if_else(!is.na(antipsy_taken_time) | !is.na(dex_taken_time), 1, 0)
         ) |>
  select(-c(antipsy_taken_time, dex_taken_time))

# Remove tibbles that won't be used moving forward
rm(gcs, sed, antipsy)
```

##### Respiratory

###### PaO~2~/FiO~2~ and SpO~2~/FiO~2~ Ratio

The Respiratory score centers on the PaO~2~ to FiO~2~ ratio (P/F ratio). The SOFA-2 document includes a clause "Use the arterial oxygen saturation (SpO~2~) to FIO~2~ ratio only when the PaO~2~:FIO~2~ ratio is unavailable and when the SpO~2~ is less than 98%." Therefore both the P/F ratio and SpO~2~ to FIO~2~ ratio (S/F ratio) will be joined. The PaO~2~ is only available from an arterial blood gas, which is not commonly obtained outside of the ICU (such as in the ED or on the ward). As such, missingness is expected for this variable.

Join the ratio of P/F ratio and S/F ratio closest to first adjunct start and within 6 hours prior. Both PaO~2~ to FiO~2~ ratio (`p_f_ratio`) and SpO~2~ to FiO~2~ ratio (`s_f_ratio`) are available in the `oxygenation` tibble. Notably, the `s_f_ratio` was only calculated if the SpO~2~ was \<98%; values \>=98% produced a missing value (NA) for `s_f_ratio`.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj,
            oxygenation |>
              filter(!is.na(p_f_ratio)) |>
              select(encounter_id, obs_time, p_f_ratio) |>
              arrange(encounter_id, obs_time, p_f_ratio) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, obs_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= obs_time),
                         first_adj_minus_6h <= obs_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(-obs_time) |>
  left_join(oxygenation |>
              filter(!is.na(s_f_ratio)) |>
              select(encounter_id, obs_time, s_f_ratio) |>
              arrange(encounter_id, obs_time, s_f_ratio) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, obs_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= obs_time),
                         first_adj_minus_6h <= obs_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  rename(first_adj_pf = p_f_ratio,
         first_adj_sf = s_f_ratio) |>
  select(-obs_time)

# Remove `oxygenation` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(oxygenation)
```

Check for missing values in `first_adj_pf` and `first_adj_sf`. Missing values are expected due to inadequate documentation of oxygen administration (resulting in no FiO~2~ available) or inability to calculate `s_f_ratio` from SpO~2~ values ≥98% (which are generally considered unreliable on the basis of the sigmoidal shape of the hemoglobin-oxygen dissociation curve values).

```{r}
round_half_up((sum(is.na(adj$first_adj_pf)) / nrow(adj)) * 100, 0)
round_half_up((sum(is.na(adj$first_adj_sf)) / nrow(adj)) * 100, 0)
```

The `adj` tibble has 38% of `first_adj_pf` values and 16% of `first_adj_sf` missing, which are reasonable for the reasons outlined above.

###### Advanced Ventilatory Support

The [SOFA-2 score calculation](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41159833/) outlines "advanced ventilatory support" as part of the respiratory sub-score, which is defined as "receipt of high-flow nasal cannula, continuous positive airflow pressure, bilevel positive airway pressure, noninvasive ventilation, invasive mechanical ventilation, or long-term home ventilation". Join advanced respiratory (ventilatory) support documented time, if the start of advanced support (`adv_resp_start`) is prior to `first_adj_time` and the end of advanced support (`adv_resp_end`) is after `first_adj_time`. Since multiple values of `adv_resp_start` are possible then arrange by time (to put latest `adv_resp_start` as first row with `desc()`) then use `distinct()` to keep only the latest `adv_resp_start` before first adjunct start.

```{r}
adj <- left_join(adj,
                 adv_resp |> select(encounter_id, adv_resp_start, adv_resp_end),
                 join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= adv_resp_start),
                         first_adj_time <= adv_resp_end),
                 relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  arrange(encounter_id, first_adj_time, desc(adv_resp_start)) |>
  distinct(encounter_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(adv_resp_before_adj = 
           factor(if_else(!is.na(adv_resp_start),
                          "Adv Resp Before Adjunct", 
                          "No Adv Resp Before Adjunct"
                          )),
         adv_resp_before_adj = 
           fct_relevel(adv_resp_before_adj, "No Adv Resp Before Adjunct")
         ) |>
  select(-c(adv_resp_start, adv_resp_end))

# Remove `adv_resp` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(adv_resp)
```

##### Cardiovascular

The Cardiovascular score centers on MAP, vasopressor or inotrope administration, and vasopressor dosage. The MAP is only considered in patients not receiving a vasopressor or inotrope. Because all patients in the cohort will be receiving norepinephrine the MAP does not need to be considered for this component. Because norepinephrine will be the only vasopressor administered at first adjunct start, other vasopressors do not need to be considered.

The highest Cardiovascular score (4 points) also includes mechanical support and the SOFA-2 document includes a clause "Any type of mechanical cardiovascular support: eg, venoarterial ECMO, intra-aortic balloon pump, left ventricular assist device, microaxial flow pump." The use of these mechanical circulatory support devices is not available in the extracted data, therefore they are not able to be considered.

The medication dobutamine is considered an inotrope and not a vasopressor, therefore it may be administered in the cohort at first adjunct start. Join dobutamine administration, if the start of dobutamine (`start_time`) is prior to `first_adj_time` and the end of dobutamine administration (`stop_time`) is after `first_adj_time`. Since multiple values of `start_time` are possible then arrange by time (to put latest `start_time` as first row with `desc()`) then use `distinct()` to keep only the latest `start_time` before first adjunct start.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  left_join(dbt |> select(encounter_id, start_time, stop_time),
            join_by(encounter_id,
                    closest(first_adj_time >= start_time),
                    first_adj_time <= stop_time),
                 relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  arrange(encounter_id, first_adj_time, desc(start_time)) |>
  distinct(encounter_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(dbt_before_adj = 
           factor(if_else(!is.na(start_time),
                          "Dobutamine Before Adjunct", 
                          "No Dobutamine Before Adjunct"
                          ))
         ) |>
  select(-c(start_time, stop_time))

# Remove `dbt` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(dbt)
```

##### Liver

Join the closest bilirubin laboratory value from the `bili` tibble, restricted to values obtained within 24 hours prior to first adjunct start.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj,
            bili |>
              select(encounter_id, bili_taken_time, bili_result) |>
              arrange(encounter_id, bili_taken_time, bili_result) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, bili_taken_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= bili_taken_time),
                         first_adj_minus_24h <= bili_taken_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  rename(first_adj_bili = bili_result) |>
  # Remove variable that won't be used moving forward
  select(-c(bili_taken_time))

# Remove `bili` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(bili)
```

##### Hemostasis

Join the closest platelets laboratory value from the `platelets` tibble, restricted to values obtained within 24 hours prior to first adjunct start.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj,
            platelets |>
              select(encounter_id, plts_taken_time, plts_result) |>
              arrange(encounter_id, plts_taken_time, plts_result) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, plts_taken_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= plts_taken_time),
                         first_adj_minus_24h <= plts_taken_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  rename(first_adj_platelets = plts_result) |>
  # Remove variable that won't be used moving forward
  select(-c(plts_taken_time))

# Remove `platelets` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(platelets)
```

##### SOFA-2 Calculation

Calculate the SOFA-2 score within each organ system, then sum to obtain the SOFA-2 at first adjunct start (`first_adj_sofa_2`). Because of the several clauses in the SOFA-2 document, the handling of these elements will be explicitly outlined below.

| Organ System | Clause (direct quote) | Management |
|:-----------------|:--------------------------|:--------------------------|
| General | For missing values at day 1, the general recommendation is to score these as 0 points. This may vary for specific purposes (eg, bedside use, research, etc). For sequential scoring, for missing data after day 1, it is to carry forward the last observation, the rationale being that nonmeasurement suggests stability. | Because first adjunct vasopressors may be started on day 1 of an encounter or subsequent days, only values obtained prior to first adjunct start were considered for scoring. The timing of values prior to first adjunct start corresponded to their typical frequency of obtainment and are outlined below. No values were carried forward and missing values will be scored as 0. |
| Brain | For sedated patients, use the last recorded GCS before sedation. If the previous GCS is unknown, score 0 | The GCS without documented administration of sedation in the preceding 6 hours was joined for `first_adj_gcs`. If `first_adj_gcs` is NA, then this sub-score will be scored as 0 |
| Brain | If receiving drug treatment for delirium (short- or long-term), score 1 point even if GCS is 15 | Drug treatment for delirium within the preceding 12 hours was joined in `delirium_med_prev_12h`, including antipsychotics and dexmedetomidine |
| Respiratory | Use the arterial oxygen saturation (SpO~2~) to FIO~2~ ratio only when the PaO~2~:FIO~2~ ratio is unavailable and when the SpO~2~ is less than 98%. Cutoffs: 0 points, greater than 300 mm Hg; 1 point, 300 mm Hg or less; 2 points, 250 mm Hg or less; 3 points, 200 mm Hg or less with ventilatory support; 4 points, 120 mm Hg or less with ventilatory support or ECMO. | Both PaO~2~ to FiO~2~ ratio (`p_f_ratio`) and SpO~2~ to FiO~2~ ratio (`s_f_ratio`) in the preceding 6 hours were joined. The `p_f_ratio` will be used preferentially, with the `s_f_ratio` only used if the `p_f_ratio` is unavailable. Notably, the `s_f_ratio` was only calculated if the SpO~2~ was \<98%; values \>=98% produced a missing value (NA) for `s_f_ratio`. |
| Respiratory | Advanced ventilatory support is defined as receipt of high-flow nasal cannula, continuous positive airflow pressure, bilevel positive airway pressure, noninvasive ventilation, invasive mechanical ventilation, or long-term home ventilation. | Advanced respiratory support device administration at first adjunct start was joined as `adv_resp_before_adj`. This variable accounted for the start and end times of device administration to ensure administration at first adjunct start. |
| Respiratory | If used for respiratory failure, ECMO (all forms) should be scored 4 in the respiratory component (regardless of PaO~2~:FIO~2~ratio), but not in the cardiovascular component. If used for cardiovascular indications (all forms), it should be automatically scored in both the cardiovascular and the respiratory systems. | ECMO use was unavailable in the dataset, therefore it cannot be considered for score calculation. |
| Cardiovascular | MAP, norepinephrine and epinephrine dosing, and inotrope and other vasopressor use are considered for scoring. | MAP is only used for scoring in patients not receiving a vasopressor or inotrope. All patients were receiving norepinephrine monotherapy at first adjunct start, therefore only norepinephrine dosing (`adj_baseline_neq`) was considered (MAP, dosing of epinephrine, and other vasopressor use were not considered). Administration of the inotrope dobutamine at first adjunct start was joined as `dbt_before_adj`. The use of other inotropes (e.g., milrinone) was not available in the dataset. |
| Cardiovascular | Vasopressor medication is only scored if given by continuous intravenous infusion for at least 1 hour | All patients received norepinephrine for at least 15 minutes prior to first adjunct start. Because first adjunct start may have been within 1 hour of norepinephrine start the minimum duration of 1 hour was not included in scoring. |
| Cardiovascular | Norepinephrine is usually dispensed as the salt (eg, hemitartrate or bitartrate). Dose should be expressed as the base. | All norepinephrine doses are expressed as the base in the dataset. |
| Cardiovascular | If dopamine is used as a single vasopressor, scoring is based on the following cutoffs: 2 points (\<=20 μg/kg/min); 3 points (\>20 to \<=40 μg/kg/min); 4 points (\>40 μg/kg/min). | No patient received dopamine as a single vasopressor in this study. |
| Cardiovascular | Any type of mechanical cardiovascular support: eg, venoarterial ECMO, intra-aortic balloon pump, left ventricular assist device, microaxial flow pump. | Mechanical circulatory (cardiovascular) support is unavailable in the dataset, therefore it cannot be considered for score calculation. |
| Kidney | Serum creatinine and urine output are considered for scoring | Serum creatinine in the preceding 24 hours was joined as `first_adj_scr`. Urine output was not considered for scoring because of known poor documentation of hourly urine output within hospital
settings. This is consistent with the approach in prior work for calculating SOFA score in patients with sepsis. ([Ginestra, Ann Thorac Soc 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35312462/), [Alrawashdeh, Crit Care Med 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38780372/)|
| Kidney | Excludes patients receiving RRT exclusively for nonrenal causes (eg, removal of toxic products, bacterial toxins, cytokines). | Patients in the dataset received RRT for renal causes. Use of RRT before first adjunct start was joined as `rrt_before_adj`. |
| Kidney | For patients receiving intermittent RRT, score 4 points on days not receiving RRT until RRT use is terminated. | The `rrt_before_adj` variable includes continuation of intermittent RRT until first adjunct start. |
| Liver | Total bilirubin is considered for scoring | Bilirubin in the preceding 24 hours was joined as `first_adj_bili`. |
| Hemostasis | Platelet count is considered for scoring | Platelets in the preceding 24 hours was joined as `first_adj_platelets`. |

First, calculate the SOFA-2 score at first adjunct start (`first_adj_sofa_2`) for reporting.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  mutate(
    sofa2_brain = case_when(
      first_adj_gcs_no_sed <= 5 ~ 4,
      first_adj_gcs_no_sed <= 8 ~ 3,
      first_adj_gcs_no_sed <= 12 ~ 2,
      first_adj_gcs_no_sed <= 14 | delirium_med_prev_12h == 1 ~ 1,
      (first_adj_gcs_no_sed == 15 & delirium_med_prev_12h == 0) |
        is.na(first_adj_gcs_no_sed) ~ 0,
      #Error code if all possibilities not accounted for
      .default = -99
      ), 
    sofa2_resp = case_when(
      first_adj_pf <=75 & 
        adv_resp_before_adj == "Adv Resp Before Adjunct" ~ 4,
      first_adj_pf <=150 & 
        adv_resp_before_adj == "Adv Resp Before Adjunct" ~ 3,
      first_adj_pf <=225 ~ 2,
      first_adj_pf <=300 ~ 1,
      first_adj_pf >300 ~ 0,
      is.na(first_adj_pf) & first_adj_sf <=120 & 
        adv_resp_before_adj == "Adv Resp Before Adjunct" ~ 4,
      is.na(first_adj_pf) & first_adj_sf <=200 & 
        adv_resp_before_adj == "Adv Resp Before Adjunct" ~ 3,
      is.na(first_adj_pf) & first_adj_sf <=250 ~ 2,
      is.na(first_adj_pf) & first_adj_sf <=300 ~ 1,
      is.na(first_adj_pf) & first_adj_sf >300 ~ 0,
      is.na(first_adj_pf) & is.na(first_adj_sf) ~ 0,
      #Error code if all possibilities not accounted for
      .default = -99
      ),
    sofa2_cv = case_when(
      adj_baseline_neq >0.4 | 
        (adj_baseline_neq >0.2 & 
           dbt_before_adj == "Dobutamine Before Adjunct"
         ) ~ 4,
      (adj_baseline_neq >0.2 &
         dbt_before_adj == "No Dobutamine Before Adjunct") |
        (adj_baseline_neq <=0.2 & 
           dbt_before_adj == "Dobutamine Before Adjunct") ~ 3,
      adj_baseline_neq <=0.2 & 
           dbt_before_adj == "No Dobutamine Before Adjunct" ~ 2,
      #Error code if all possibilities not accounted for
      .default = -99
      ),
    sofa2_liver = case_when(
      first_adj_bili <= 1.2 | is.na(first_adj_bili) ~ 0,
      first_adj_bili <= 3 ~ 1,
      first_adj_bili <= 6 ~ 2,
      first_adj_bili <= 12 ~ 3,
      first_adj_bili > 12 ~ 4,
      #Error code if all possibilities not accounted for
      .default = -99
      ),
    sofa2_kidney = case_when(
      #Need to adjudicate in this order to ensure correct scoring
      rrt_before_adj == "RRT Before Adjunct" ~ 4,
      first_adj_scr >3.5 ~ 3,
      first_adj_scr <=1.2 | is.na(first_adj_scr) ~ 0,
      first_adj_scr <=2 ~ 1,
      first_adj_scr <=3.5 ~ 2,
      #Error code if all possibilities not accounted for
      .default = -99
      ),
    sofa2_hemostasis = case_when(
      #Need to adjudicate in this order to ensure correct scoring
      first_adj_platelets <=50 ~ 4,
      first_adj_platelets <=80 ~ 3,
      first_adj_platelets <=100 ~ 2,
      first_adj_platelets <=150 ~ 1,
      first_adj_platelets >150 | is.na(first_adj_platelets) ~ 0,
      #Error code if all possibilities not accounted for
      .default = -99
      )
    )
```

Show distribution of SOFA-2 score components to ensure no score was calculated with the error code (-99) and values match expectations.

```{r}
describe(adj |> select(sofa2_brain, sofa2_resp, sofa2_cv, sofa2_liver, sofa2_kidney, sofa2_hemostasis))
```

No score component was calculated with the error code and values match expectations, including `sofa2_cv` only ranging from values 2 to 4. Move on to calculation of the SOFA-2 score (`first_adj_sofa_2`) and show the distribution of the score to ensure expectations are met.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(first_adj_sofa_2 = sofa2_brain + sofa2_resp + sofa2_cv +
           sofa2_liver + sofa2_kidney + sofa2_hemostasis
         ) |>
  ungroup()
describe(adj$first_adj_sofa_2)
```

The minimum value of the score is 2 points, which matches expectations because the minimum value for the Cardiovascular component is 2 in this cohort. It is not unexpected to have a maximum value of 22 (instead of 24) at first adjunct start since this time point may be relatively early in a patient's septic shock disease progression.

Finally, calculate the SOFA-2 score without the cardiovascular component at first adjunct start (`first_adj_sofa_2_no_cv`) for use in modeling. This variable is needed because of the intent to incorporate norepinephrine dose at first adjunct start (`adj_baseline_neq`) as a variable in the model (to avoid collinearity between the two variables). Then show the distribution of `first_adj_sofa_2_no_cv`.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(first_adj_sofa_2_no_cv = sofa2_brain + sofa2_resp + sofa2_liver + 
           sofa2_kidney + sofa2_hemostasis
         ) |>
  ungroup()
describe(adj$first_adj_sofa_2_no_cv)
```

The distribution of `first_adj_sofa_2_no_cv`, with 0 as the lowest value and 19 as the maximum (since 20 would be the maximum possible value without the Cardiovascular component).

#### Mechanical Ventilation

Join mechanical ventilation documented time, if the start of mechanical ventilation (`mv_start`) is prior to `first_adj_time` and the end of mechanical ventilation (`mv_end`) is after `first_adj_time`. Since multiple values of `mv_start` are possible then arrange by time (to put latest `mv_start` as first row with desc()) then use distinct() to keep only the latest `mv_start` before first adjunct start.

```{r}
adj <- left_join(adj,
                mv |> select(encounter_id, mv_start, mv_end),
                join_by(encounter_id,
                        closest(first_adj_time >= mv_start),
                        first_adj_time <= mv_end),
                relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  arrange(encounter_id, first_adj_time, desc(mv_start)) |>
  distinct(encounter_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(mv_before_adj = 
           factor(if_else(!is.na(mv_start),
                          "MV Before Adjunct", "No MV Before Adjunct")),
         mv_before_adj = 
           fct_relevel(mv_before_adj, "No MV Before Adjunct")
         ) |>
  select(-c(mv_start, mv_end))

# Remove `mv` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(mv)
```

#### Arterial pH

Join arterial pH values closest to first adjunct start and within 6 hours prior. Measured pH values from an arterial blood gas will be used preferentially. However, arterial pH values are commonly unavailable in patients outside of the intensive care unit and venous pH is used as a reasonable clinical surrogate when a correction factor is applied [Byrne 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24383789/). Therefore, when a measured arterial pH value is unavailable, use a calculated arterial pH value from a venous sample.

Both measured arterial pH (`pH_result`) and calculated arterial pH from a venous sample (`pH_result_calc`) are available in the `pH` tibble. In the call below, join both the closest value for `pH_result` and `pH_result_calc` at first adjunct start, then populate the `first_adj_pH` variable with `pH_result` when available, if not `pH_result_calc` when available.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj,
            pH |>
              select(encounter_id, pH_taken_time, pH_result) |>
              arrange(encounter_id, pH_taken_time, pH_result) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, pH_taken_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= pH_taken_time),
                         first_adj_minus_6h <= pH_taken_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(-pH_taken_time) |>
  left_join(pH |>
              select(encounter_id, pH_taken_time, pH_result_calc) |>
              arrange(encounter_id, pH_taken_time, pH_result_calc) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, pH_taken_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= pH_taken_time),
                         first_adj_minus_6h <= pH_taken_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(first_adj_pH = coalesce(pH_result, pH_result_calc)) |>
  # Remove variables that won't be used moving forward
  select(-c(pH_taken_time, pH_result, pH_result_calc))

# Remove `pH` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(pH)
```

#### Temperature

Join the closest temperature value (`temp_c`) from the `temperature` tibble, restricted to values obtained within 6 hours prior to first adjunct start.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj,
            temperature |>
              select(encounter_id, temp_time, temp_c) |>
              arrange(encounter_id, temp_time, temp_c) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, temp_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= temp_time),
                         first_adj_minus_6h <= temp_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  rename(first_adj_temp_c = temp_c) |>
  # Remove variable that won't be used moving forward
  select(-c(temp_time))

# Remove `temperature` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(temperature)
```

#### Heart Rate

Join the closest heart rate value (`hr`) from the `heart_rate` tibble, restricted to values obtained within 6 hours prior to first adjunct start. Since all patients had a perfusing heart rhythm at the time of first adjunct start, filter out `hr` values \<20 bpm or \>200 bpm prior to joining the data since these values are likely erroneous (confirmed on random review of values).

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj,
            heart_rate |>
              filter(hr >=20 & hr <=200) |>
              select(encounter_id, hr_time, hr) |>
              arrange(encounter_id, hr_time, hr) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, hr_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= hr_time),
                         first_adj_minus_6h <= hr_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  rename(first_adj_heart_rate = hr) |>
  # Remove variable that won't be used moving forward
  select(-c(hr_time))

# Remove `heart_rate` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(heart_rate)
```

#### Respiratory Rate

Join the closest respiratory rate value (`rr`) from the `resp_rate` tibble, restricted to values obtained within 6 hours prior to first adjunct start. Since all patients had a perfusing heart rhythm at the time of first adjunct start, filter out `rr` values \<10 breaths per minute or \>70 breaths per minute prior to joining the data since these values are likely erroneous (confirmed on random review of values).

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj,
            resp_rate |>
              filter(rr >=10 & rr <=70) |>
              select(encounter_id, rr_time, rr) |>
              arrange(encounter_id, rr_time, rr) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, rr_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= rr_time),
                         first_adj_minus_6h <= rr_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  rename(first_adj_resp_rate = rr) |>
  # Remove variable that won't be used moving forward
  select(-c(rr_time))

# Remove `resp_rate` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(resp_rate)
```

#### Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP)

Join the closest MAP value (`closest_map`) at first adjunct start, which was already adjudicated for each vasopressor dose above in the `pressors_doses` tibble. Note that this is the closest MAP value within 3 hours of first adjunct start.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj,
            pressors_doses |>
              select(encounter_id, mar_taken_time, closest_map),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         first_adj_time == mar_taken_time),
            relationship = "one-to-many"
            ) |>
  distinct(encounter_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  rename(first_adj_map = closest_map)
```

#### Lactate

Join the closest lactate lab value (`lactate_result`) from the `lactate` tibble, restricted to values obtained within 12 hours prior to first adjunct start. The rationale for selecting a window of 12 hours before first adjunct start (instead of a shorter window such as 6 hours used with other variables) is because relatively low values may not be followed serially resulting in sparse sampling.

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(adj |> 
              mutate(first_adj_minus_12h = first_adj_time - dhours(12)),
            lactate |>
              select(encounter_id, lactate_taken_time, lactate_result) |>
              arrange(encounter_id, lactate_taken_time, lactate_result) |>
              distinct(encounter_id, lactate_taken_time, .keep_all = TRUE),
            by = join_by(encounter_id,
                         closest(first_adj_time >= lactate_taken_time),
                         first_adj_minus_12h <= lactate_taken_time
                         ),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  rename(first_adj_lactate = lactate_result) |>
  # Remove variable that won't be used moving forward
  select(-c(lactate_taken_time))

# Remove `lactate` tibble because it won't be used moving forward
rm(lactate)
```

#### Fluid Boluses

Determine the cumulative volume of fluid boluses administered within the 12 hours prior to first adjunct start. First, join the `first_adj_time` and `first_adj_minus_12h` vectors from the `adj` tibble to the `fluids` tibble. Since this relationship is expected to have a "many-to-one" relationship, specify it in the call. Then, determine if the fluid administration date/time (`mar_taken_time`) was within the outlined time range. Lastly, only retain observations meeting these criteria and remove vectors that will not be used moving forward.

```{r}
fluids_adj <- fluids |>
  left_join(adj |> select(encounter_id, first_adj_time, first_adj_minus_12h),
            join_by(encounter_id),
            relationship = "many-to-one"
            ) |>
  mutate(within_prior_12h = 
           if_else(mar_taken_time >= first_adj_minus_12h & 
                     mar_taken_time <= first_adj_time, "Yes", "No")
         ) |>
  filter(within_prior_12h == "Yes")
```

Next, calculate the cumulative sum of the fluid bolus volume administered (`vol_mL`) per `encounter_id` in a new vector (`fluid_mL_12h_prior_adj`).

```{r}
fluids_adj  <- fluids_adj  |>
  group_by(encounter_id) |>
  mutate(fluid_mL_12h_prior_adj = cumsum(vol_mL)) |>
  ungroup() 
```

Lastly, join the largest value of the `fluid_mL_12h_prior_adj` vector per observation (representing the cumulative volume of fluid administered within the 12 hours prior to first adjunct start) to the `adj` tibble. Some patients (`encounter_id`s) were not present in the `fluids_adj` tibble because they did not have fluid boluses administered within the 12 hours prior to vasopressor start. In these cases the `fluid_mL_12h_prior_adj` vector will have a value of "NA" after the join. Replace these "NA" values with zero as part of the call.

```{r}
adj <- left_join(adj,
                fluids_adj  |>
                  arrange(encounter_id, desc(fluid_mL_12h_prior_adj)) |>
                  select(encounter_id, fluid_mL_12h_prior_adj) |>
                  distinct(encounter_id, .keep_all = TRUE),
                join_by(encounter_id),
                relationship = "one-to-one"
                ) |>
  mutate(fluid_mL_12h_prior_adj = replace_na(fluid_mL_12h_prior_adj, 0),
         fluid_mL_kg_12h_prior_adj = fluid_mL_12h_prior_adj / first_adj_wt_kg
         ) |>
  rename(first_adj_fluid_mL = fluid_mL_12h_prior_adj,
         first_adj_fluid_mL_kg = fluid_mL_kg_12h_prior_adj
         )
# Remove fluids tibbles since they won't be used moving forward
rm(fluids, fluids_adj)
```

#### Steroids

Determine the presence of at least one parenteral or enteral dose of any glucocorticoid medication administered within the 24 hour period prior to first adjunct start. All observations in the `steroids` tibble represent parenteral or enteral administration of a glucocorticoid medication (also known as a "corticosteroid", or, simply "steroid").

First, join the `first_adj_time` and `first_adj_minus_24h` variables from the `adj` tibble to the `steroids` tibble.

```{r}
steroids <- left_join(steroids,
                      adj |> select(encounter_id, first_adj_time,
                                      first_adj_minus_24h
                                    ) |>
                        distinct(),
                      join_by(encounter_id),
                      relationship = "many-to-one")
```

Next, assess steroid administration within the outlined time period (between 24 hours prior to first adjunct start and first adjunct start) based on the steroid MAR taken time.

```{r}
steroids <- steroids |>
  mutate(during_window = if_else(mar_taken_time >= first_adj_minus_24h &
                                   mar_taken_time <= first_adj_time,
                                 "Yes", "No")) |>
  filter(during_window == "Yes")
```

Lastly, create a vector within the `adj` tibble for steroid administration during the outlined time period (`first_adj_steroid`) and remove the `steroid` tibble because it won't be used moving forward.

```{r}
adj <- adj |>
  mutate(first_adj_steroid = 
           factor(if_else(encounter_id %in% steroids$encounter_id,
                          "Steroids", "No Steroids"
                          ))
         )
rm(steroids)
```

#### LVEF {#sec-lvef}

Join left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) within the 30 days prior to adjunct start. Ideally only the LVEF after norepinephrine initiation (and prior to adjunct start) would be used, but if this approach were to be used the missingness percentage would be unreasonable for an imputation model (85%, data not shown).

```{r}
adj <- 
  left_join(
    adj |> mutate(first_adj_minus_30d = first_adj_time - ddays(30)),
    lvef |> select(patient_id, observation_date, lvef),
    join_by(patient_id,
            closest(first_adj_time >= observation_date),
            first_adj_minus_30d <= observation_date),
    relationship = "one-to-many") |>
  arrange(encounter_id, desc(observation_date)) |>
  distinct(encounter_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(encounter_id, admission_time) |>
  select(-first_adj_minus_30d, observation_date) |>
  rename(first_adj_lvef = lvef)

# Remove the `lvef` tibble since it won't be used moving forward
rm(lvef) 
```

Show missignness percentage in the `first_adj_lvef` column.

```{r}
round_half_up((sum(is.na(adj$first_adj_lvef))/nrow(adj))*100,0)
```

In all patients who received an adjunctive vasopressor regimen, 61% were missing an LVEF measurement within 30 days prior to adjunct start. This missingness percentage is not ideal, but at a reasonable level to move forward.

# Sample Size Calculation

The prevalence of positive response to adjunctive vasopressors is unclear. Previous data using similar criteria ranged from 40-45% for vasopressin ([Sacha 2018](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2110582025008039?via%3Dihub), [Sacha 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34582425/)) and was 25% for epinephrine in one study ([Ammar 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31202160/)). Yet, no studies exist for response to phenylephrine. Because phenylephrine and epinephrine are catecholamine analogs that activate the adrenergic alpha-1 receptor similar to norepinephrine, their adjunctive use may lead to less frequent blood pressure response. Therefore, for the sample size calculation will use a lower response prevalence estimate (30%).

For a binary categorical outcome (`response`), assuming outcome prevalence 0.3, expected C-statistic 0.75, shrinkage 0.9, and 15 candidate predictor parameters, calculate the minimum sample size using `pmsampsize()` from the `{pmsampsize}` package.

```{r}
pmsampsize(type = "b",
           parameters = 15,
           prevalence = 0.3,
           cstatistic = 0.75
           )
```

Each derivation (first adjunctive vasopressor use) cohort will need at least 771 included patients to have adequate power to estimate a clinical prediction model (with the above assumptions).

# Eligibility Criteria {#sec-elig}

The goal of this work is to predict second-line (first adjunctive) vasopressor response in patients with septic shock receiving norepinephrine. Eligibility criteria will be outlined below and subsequently applied in a code chunk.

1)  Adults (age ≥18 years) with septic shock per clinical criteria (CDC Adult Sepsis Event and/or Sepsis-3)
    -   Restricted to the first sepsis episode on the patient level
2)  Norepinephrine as initial therapy
3)  Norepinephrine duration ≥15 minutes
4)  Norepinephrine monotherapy duration ≥15 minutes
    -   Each of these first four criteria were implemented in the prior work to create the imported `ne_incl` tibble.
5)  Adjunctive vasopressor receipt
    -   Initiation of a non-norepinephrine vasopressor and documentation of a non-zero norepinephrine dosage at the time of non-norepinephrine vasopressor initiation
6)  Second-line (first adjunctive) vasopressor administration of vasopressin, epinephrine, or phenylephrine
    -   Although the use of adjunctive phenylephrine is not recommended for or against by the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines, it is often used in clinical practice - particularly for patients with tachycardia/tachyarrhythmias on norepinephrine or as an alternative to vasopressin due to lower cost. Phenylephrine use notations in Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline iterations that were released during the study time period are outlined below
    -   2008: Recommendation: "We suggest that epinephrine, phenylephrine, or vasopressin should not be administered as the initial vasopressor in septic shock." (No recommendation regarding adjunct use.). Text body: "Phenylephrine is the adrenergic agent least likely to produce tachycardia but as a pure vasopressor would be expected to decrease stroke volume."
    -   2012: Recommendation: "Phenylephrine is not recommended in the treatment of septic shock except in circumstances where (a) norepinephrine is associated with serious arrhythmias, (b) cardiac output is known to be high and blood pressure persistently low, or (c) as salvage therapy when combined inotrope/vasopressor drugs and low-dose vasopressin have failed to achieve MAP target"
    -   2016: No recommendation. Text body: "A network meta-analysis resulted in imprecise estimates (wide confidence intervals) when phenylephrine was compared to other vasopressors (281). Therefore, the impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain, and phenylephrine use should be limited until more research is available."
    -   2021: No recommendation. Not mentioned in text body.

In the call below, adjudicate and tabulate eligibility criteria.

```{r}
ne_incl <- ne_incl |> 
  left_join(adj |> select(encounter_id, adj_baseline_neq),
            by = join_by(encounter_id),
            relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(elig = case_when(
    event_3_level_type != "1-adjunct" ~ "exclude-1_no_adjunct",
    first_adj %notin% c("vasopressin", "epinephrine", "phenylephrine") ~
      "exclude-2_adjunct_regimen_not_of_interest",
    adj_baseline_neq == 0 ~ "exclude-3_not_adjunctive;baseline_neq_zero",
    .default = "include"
    )) |>
  select(-adj_baseline_neq)

ne_incl |> 
  tabyl(elig, shock_onset_hosp_state) |> 
  adorn_totals(where = c("row", "col")) |> 
  adorn_percentages(denominator = "col")|>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |>
  adorn_ns(position = "front") |>
  adorn_title(placement = "combined") |>
  kable(align = c('lcc'),
        caption = "Eligibility Adjudication"
        ) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

Variables of interest were transformed or joined to the `adj` tibble, which only includes patients who received adjunctive vasopressors. Use this tibble and apply the other eligibility criterion to create analytic tibble (`incl`). Then show the number of observations in the `incl` tibble to ensure the numbers align with above.

```{r}
incl <- adj |>
  filter(first_adj %in% c("vasopressin", "epinephrine", "phenylephrine") &
           adj_baseline_neq != 0
           ) |>
  droplevels()

count(incl, .by = shock_onset_hosp_state) |>
  rename("State" = .by) |>
  kable(align = c('lc'),
        caption = "Included Count"
        ) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

The counts match, therefore continue with the analysis.

Show the first adjunctive vasopressor received in included patients by cohort.
