# Outcome Measure Assessment

Describe outcome measure components by first adjunctive vasopressor by state.

```{r}
incl |>
  tabyl(response_type, first_adj, first_adj_hosp_state) |>
  adorn_totals(where = c("row", "col")) |> 
  adorn_percentages(denominator = "col")|>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |>
  adorn_ns(position = "front")
```

As noted in @sec-out, the 49 observations (47 and 2 observations in the Ohio and Florida cohorts, respectively) with missing MAP data were considered as not meeting criteria for response. Show the outcomes with this response type collapsed with the "0-no_resp_map_below_65" category.

```{r}
(out_by_cohort <- incl |>
   select(response_type, first_adj, first_adj_hosp_state) |>
   mutate(response_type = case_when(
     response_type == "2-resp_unclear_map_missing" ~ 
       "0-no_resp_map_below_65_or_missing",
     response_type == "0-no_resp_map_below_65" ~ 
       "0-no_resp_map_below_65_or_missing",
     .default = response_type
     ),
     response_type = fct_relevel(response_type, "1-response", 
                                 "0-no_resp_neq_same_or_higher",
                                 "0-no_resp_map_below_65_or_missing",
                                 "0-no_resp_death"
                                 )
     ) |>
   tbl_strata(
     strata = first_adj_hosp_state,
     .tbl_fun = 
       ~ .x |>
       tbl_summary(by = first_adj, missing = "no",
                   statistic = all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)",
                   digits = all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
                   ) |>
       add_overall()
    ) |>
    modify_fmt_fun(
     all_stat_cols() ~ function(x) gsub("%", "", x)
     ))
```

As noted in @sec-out, the incidence of response after vasopressin initiation (34% and 28%, respectively, in the Derivation and Validation cohorts) is lower than in previous work from our research team with vasopressin (40%), but is reasonably close. The difference is explainable because patients and criteria in the previous work were slightly different - in this work all patients received initial norepinephrine (previously all initial vasopressors were included), death between first adjunct start and 6 hours later was considered non-response (not considered in prior work), the vasopressor contribution of vasopressin (equated through the Kotani norepinephrine-equivalent dose \[NEQ\]) was considered in the response criteria (previously it was ignored), and the NEQ was required to be lower than baseline (not lower or equal to baseline since the vasopressin NEQ contribution was considered). Inclusion of the vasopressor contribution of vasopressin as part of the NEQ is likely the largest driver of the difference in response incidence between studies.

Compare response frequency by first adjunctive vasopressor in the derivation (Ohio) cohort.

```{r}
incl |> 
  filter(first_adj_hosp_state == "Ohio") |>
  tabyl(first_adj, response) |>
  janitor::chisq.test()

glm(response ~ first_adj,
    data = incl |> filter(first_adj_hosp_state == "Ohio"),
    family = binomial(link = "logit")
    ) |>
  tidy(exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  select(term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value) |>
  mutate(term = sub("^first_adj", "", term)) |>
  kable(align = c('lcccc'), digits = 2) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

Compared with vasopressin, receipt of epinephrine as the first adjunctive vasopressor was associated with 34% lower odds of hemodynamic response at 6 hours (OR 0.76, 95% CI; 0.64, 0.89). There was no substantial difference in response between phenylephrine and vasopressin (OR 1.09, 95% CI; 0.94, 1.27).

Determine the association of adjunctive vasopressor response with hospital mortality in the derivation and validation cohorts.

```{r}
incl |> 
  filter(first_adj_hosp_state == "Ohio") |>
  mutate(response = fct_relevel(response, "Response")) |>
  with(table(response, mort_hosp)) |> 
  Epi::twoby2()

incl |> 
  filter(first_adj_hosp_state == "Florida") |>
  mutate(response = fct_relevel(response, "Response")) |>
  with(table(response, mort_hosp)) |> 
  Epi::twoby2()
```

In the derivation cohort, in the 2,369 patients who had hemodynamic response at 6 hours, hospital mortality was lower (n = 1051 [42.4%]) compared with the 4,554 patients without response (n = 2,555 [56.1%]; unadjusted OR 0.62 [95% CI 0.56, 0.69]). Findings were similar in the validation cohort, where hospital mortality developed in 117 of 314 patients with hemodynamic response (37.3%) versus 371 of 808 (45.9%) patients without hemodynamic response (unadjusted OR 0.70 [95% CI 0.54, 0.91]).

Use a simple logistic regression model to determine risk-adjusted odds ratio for mortality with adjunctive vasopressor response. In these models, use the complete SOFA-2 score for risk adjustment.

```{r}
glm(mort_hosp == "Died" ~ response + age + elixhauser_index + first_adj_sofa_2,
    data = incl |> filter(first_adj_hosp_state == "Ohio"),
    family = binomial(link = "logit")
    ) |>
  tidy(exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  select(term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high) |>
  rename(OR = estimate) |>
  mutate(term = sub("^response", "", term))

glm(mort_hosp == "Died" ~ response + age + elixhauser_index + first_adj_sofa_2,
    data = incl |> filter(first_adj_hosp_state == "Florida"),
    family = binomial(link = "logit")
    ) |>
  tidy(exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  select(term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high) |>
  rename(OR = estimate) |>
  mutate(term = sub("^response", "", term))
```

# Codebook and Data Description

## Create Derivation and Validation Datasets

Included cases will be divided into a derivation cohort from Ohio (`oh`) and an external validation cohort from Florida (`fl`).

```{r}
oh <- incl |> filter(first_adj_hosp_state == "Ohio")

fl <- incl |> filter(first_adj_hosp_state == "Florida")
```

Verify number of observations in each tibble matches expectations.

```{r}
nrow(oh)
nrow(fl)
```

The number of observations is correct (6,934 in the derivation [`oh`] dataset and 1,128 in the validation [`fl`] dataset).

## Selecting Model Variables

Here, create an analytic tibble with only the variables that will be used for model derivation. In this process, vector names will also be adjusted for ease moving forward. The `race_eth` vector will be included for future use as a part of fairness checks for the final model, but the variable **will not** be included as a predictor in the models.

Each candidate predictor was selected based on clinical knowledge and biological plausibility for influencing the outcome (adjunctive vasopressor response) based on input from investigators, who are domain experts. Further, predictor variables were assimilated based on a review of the literature ([Sacha 2018](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2110582025008039?via%3Dihub), [Bauer 2022](https://doi.org/10.1097/CCE.0000000000000634), [Dugar 2023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcrc.2023.154298), [Sacha 2023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chest.2023.07.009)). Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; `lvef`) was considered as a candidate predictor based on [Dugar 2023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcrc.2023.154298). Considering the limitations of the variable outlined in @sec-lvef (timing of within 30 days prior to adjunct instead of after norepinephrine initiation and relatively high missingness), this variable was omitted. As surrogates for LVEF, history of heart failure (`heart_failure`) and treatment unit (`tx_unit`) with preservation of "Cardiac ICU" as a category level (due to frequent treatment of patients with low LVEF in that unit type) were utilized.

The candidate predictors and number of candidate predictor parameters were constrained to those that could be supported across all adjunctive vasopressor treatment cohorts. **In a sensitivity analysis, expansion of the vasopressin model from 15 to 29 degrees of freedom produced negligible improvement in discrimination and overall performance, supporting use of the common predictor set for all treatment-specific models.**

```{r}
incl_mod_var <- oh |>
  select(response, first_adj, age, sex, race_eth, heart_failure, 
         tx_unit = first_adj_tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
         sofa2_no_cv = first_adj_sofa_2_no_cv, 
         pH = first_adj_pH, neq = adj_baseline_neq, 
         shock_dur_h = hours_to_first_adj, map = first_adj_map, 
         lactate = first_adj_lactate
         )
```

Next, verify variable structure.

```{r}
str(incl_mod_var, vec.len = 0)
```

The variables each have the intended structure, however some factor variables need re-leveled to place the intended baseline (reference) category first. Also, collapse the levels for some categorical variables.

```{r}
incl_mod_var <- incl_mod_var |>
  mutate(response = fct_relevel(response, "Response", "No Response"),
         tx_unit = factor(if_else(tx_unit == "Surgical ICU" |
                                    tx_unit == "Mixed Med/Surg ICU",
                                  "Surgical or Mixed Med/Surg ICU",
                                  tx_unit
                                  ),
                          levels = c("Medical ICU", "Cardiac ICU",
                                     "ED/Rapid Response", 
                                     "Surgical or Mixed Med/Surg ICU"
                                     )),
         ssc_era = factor(if_else(ssc_era == "SSC 2021", 
                                  "SSC 2021", 
                                  "Before SSC 2021"
                                  ),
                          levels = c("Before SSC 2021", "SSC 2021")
                          ),
         criteria_met = factor(if_else(criteria_met == "ASE only", 
                                       "ASE only",
                                       "Both or Sepsis-3 only"
                                       ),
                               levels = c("ASE only", "Both or Sepsis-3 only")
                               )
         )
```

Verify variable structure after changes.

```{r}
str(incl_mod_var, vec.len = 0)
```

## Codebook

The codebook below outlines variables that will be used for prediction model derivation and validation. The baseline (reference) category for categorical predictors is listed first. All predictor (independent) variables were available at the time of first adjunctive vasopressor initiation. Missing values are outlined in @sec-miss-oh and @sec-miss-fl and managed within the model building steps. Note that `age`, `sex`, and `race_eth` are included in the `incl_mod_var` tibble for subsequent fairness checks, but will **not** be utilized as a predictor (rather, they will be in a "bystander" role in the models).

| Variable | Role | Type | Description |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| `response` | outcome | 2-cat | Response, No Response: Response or not (No Response) to first adjunctive vasopressor initiation. Response is defined as achieving mean arterial pressure (MAP) ≥65 mm Hg with a decrease from baseline in norepinephrine-equivalent dosage at 6 hours after first adjunctive vasopressor initiation. |
| `first_adj` | identifier | 3-cat | vasopressin, epinephrine, phenylephrine: First adjunctive vasopressor initiated. Used as a cohort identifier for data splitting. |
| `heart_failure` | predictor | 2-cat | No, Yes: Absence (No) or presence (Yes) of chronic heart failure (per Elixhauser criteria) at admission. |
| `tx_unit` | predictor | 4-cat | Medical ICU, Cardiac ICU, ED/Rapid Response, Surgical or Mixed Med/Surg ICU: Treatment unit at first adjunctive vasopressor initiation, whether medical intensive care unit (ICU; Medical ICU), cardiac ICU (Cardiac ICU), emergency department/rapid response team (ED/Rapid Response), or surgical/mixed medical-surgical ICU (Mixed Med/Surg ICU). |
| `ssc_era` | predictor | 2-cat | Before SSC 2021, SSC 2021: Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) Guideline treatment "era" based on the patient admission date and guideline publication date, whether before publication of the 2021 SSC guidelines (Before SSC 2021) or after publication of the 2021 SSC guidelines (SSC 2021). |
| `criteria_met` | predictor | 2-cat | ASE only, Both or Sepsis-3 only: Clinical criteria for septic shock met, whether CDC Adult Sepsis Event (ASE) only (ASE only) or both CDC ASE and Sepsis-3 or Sepsis-3 only (Both or Sepsis-3 only). |
| `sofa2_no_cv` | predictor | quant | Sequential Organ Failure Assessment(SOFA)-2 score without the cardiovascular sub-score component at first adjunctive vasopressor initiation. |
| `pH` | predictor | quant | Arterial pH, value at the time of first adjunctive vasopressor initiation. |
| `neq` | predictor | quant | Norepinephrine dosage (mcg/kg/min), value at the time of first adjunctive vasopressor initiation. |
| `shock_dur_h` | predictor | quant | Duration (hours) of norepinephrine monotherapy administration at the time of first adjunctive vasopressor initiation. |
| `map` | predictor | quant | Mean arterial pressure (mm Hg), closest value (within 6 hours prior) at the time of first adjunctive vasopressor initiation. |
| `lactate` | predictor | quant | Lactate concentration (mg/dL), closest value (within 12 hours prior) at the time of first adjunctive vasopressor initiation. |

## Missing Values {#sec-miss-oh}

Missing values will be outlined here. An *a priori* threshold for allowable missingness will not be utilized. Based on the TRIPOD+AI guidelines [Collins 2024](https://www.bmj.com/content/385/bmj-2023-078378.long), the number of missing values per variable will be described and the details of the imputation method reported.

First, evaluate for missing data in the outcome variable.

```{r}
incl_mod_var |> select(response) |>
  miss_var_summary() |> mutate(pct_miss = as.numeric(pct_miss)) |> 
  kable(digits = 3, 
        caption = "Missingness in Outcome in Derivation (Ohio) Data"
        ) |> 
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

There are no missing values in the outcome variable.

Next, evaluate for missing data in the predictors of interest by first adjunctive vasopressor medication. Notably, since race/ethnicity (`race_eth`) will not be a predictor in models it will be omitted from this assessment.

```{r}
incl_mod_var |> 
  select(-c(response, age, sex, race_eth)) |>
  group_by(first_adj) |>
  miss_var_summary() |> 
  mutate(pct_miss = as.numeric(pct_miss)) |> 
  kable(digits = 1, 
        caption = "Missingness in Predictors in Derivation (Ohio) Data"
        ) |> 
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

There are missing data in the `pH`, `lactate`, and `map` variables for each first adjunctive vasopressor, which need to be managed. Missing data will be imputed with regression (single) imputation instead of multiple imputation to mimic model deployment in an electronic health record where model derivation data are inaccessible. [Sisk 2023](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/09622802231165001). Missing data will be imputed under a missing-at-random assumption and the outcome will not be utilized as a variable in the imputation model. Since each of the variables with missing data is continuous (numeric), these predictors will be imputed with linear regression. Because the measurement of predictors is likely to vary across settings (locations) and over time (and therefore the missingness mechanism is not stable), a missing indicator will not be incorporated, as recommended by [van Smeden 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32565213/) and [Sisk 2023](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/09622802231165001). Missing data will be imputed sing the {tidymodels} `recipe::step_impute_linear()` function within each first adjunctive vasopressor cohort in order to avoid data leakage between cohorts.

Assess missingness patterns.

```{r}
incl_mod_var |>
  count(
    pH_missing = is.na(pH),
    lactate_missing = is.na(lactate),
    map_missing = is.na(map)
    )
```

Since there is some overlap in missingness (particularly for `pH` and `lactate`), imputation will be done sequentially to maximize available information.

# Prediction Model Building and Evaluation

Clinical prediction models will be developed and evaluated using the `{tidymodels}` meta-package (with the `{bonsai}` extension package, as needed).

## Split Data

Within the derivation (Ohio) dataset, create separate cohorts for building models based on the first adjunctive vasopressor (`first_adj`), whether vasopressin (`avp`), epinephrine (`epi`), or phenylephrine (`pe`). Then confirm that the observation count in the `oh` tibble matches the sum of the count in the individual tibbles.

```{r}
avp <- incl_mod_var |> filter(first_adj == "vasopressin") |> select(-first_adj)
epi <- incl_mod_var |> filter(first_adj == "epinephrine") |> select(-first_adj)
pe <- incl_mod_var |> filter(first_adj == "phenylephrine") |> select(-first_adj)

nrow(incl_mod_var) == (nrow(avp) + nrow(epi) + nrow(pe))
```

## Vasopressin {#sec-avp}

This section will build and evaluate prediction models for response after initiation of vasopressin as the first adjunctive vasopressor. 

### Logistic Regression

Here, use logistic regression to generate prediction models using two approaches: 1) main effects (additive) only, and 2) non-linear effects of predictors.

#### Main Effects

Create the model specifications using the {parsnip} package here.

```{r}
lr_spec <- 
  logistic_reg() |>
  set_engine("glm")
```

Create a basic (main effects) {parsnip} `recipe()` object for the model. Include a step for imputation of missing predictors (`map`, `lactate`, and `pH` in that sequence due to their missingness levels and patterns).

```{r}
avp_m1_lr_rec_main <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = avp) |>
  # Declare age, sex, and race_eth in a bystander role to keep it in the 
  # resampling dataset for future use in fairness checks
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  # Single (linear regression) imputation for missing quantitatitve predictors
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h
                       )
                     ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map
                       )
    ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate
                       )
    )
```

Now set workflow by adding the model specification and formula. 

```{r}
avp_m1_lr_main_wflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(avp_m1_lr_rec_main) |>
  add_model(lr_spec) 
```

Fit model.

```{r}
avp_m1_lr_main_fit <-
  fit(avp_m1_lr_main_wflow, data = avp)
```

Check the number of parameters in this fitted model.

```{r}
avp_m1_fit_obj <- extract_fit_engine(avp_m1_lr_main_fit)

avp_m1_fit_obj$rank - 1 # Subtract 1 to remove the intercept from the count
rm(avp_m1_fit_obj)
```

There are 12 predictor parameters (degrees of freedom) in this model with only main effects, therefore non-linear terms can be explored.

The metrics for this model will be generated and assessed in the next section.

#### Transformations of Predictors

Here consider transformations of the predictors to discern if non-linear terms for the predictors will improve the fit of the model.

Generate a plot of Spearman's $\rho^2$ rank correlation to show variables with highest potential ability to improve the model predictive performance through introduction of a non-linear term as described by Harrell in [*Regression Modeling Strategies, 2nd edition*](https://hbiostat.org/rmsc/psmcase).

```{r}
plot(spearman2(response ~ ., data = avp |> select(-c(age, sex, race_eth))))

invisible(pdf("avp_spearman.pdf"))
plot(spearman2(response ~ ., data = avp |> select(-c(age, sex, race_eth))),
     main = ""
     )
title(main = expression("Vasopressin Spearman " * rho^2))
invisible(dev.off())
```

The Spearman's $\rho^2$ rank correlation plot shows that `neq` has the highest $\rho^2$, indicating `neq` has the highest potential ability to improve the model predictive performance through introduction of a non-linear term. Since `neq` is quantitative variable, introduce non-linearity with a natural spline with 3 knots (4 degrees of freedom). This approach will add three degrees of freedom to the main effects model (which had 12 parameter degrees of freedom) for a total of 15 parameter degrees of freedom (our budget amount based on the sample size calculation). 

In the call below add the natural spline term to determine if it improve model fit. For this work, use a `workflow_set()` for the within-model comparisons.

```{r}
avp_m1_lr_rec_ns <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = avp) |>
  # Declare age, sex, and race_eth in a bystander role to keep it in the 
  # resampling dataset for future use in fairness checks
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  # Single (linear regression) imputation for missing quantitatitve predictors
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, 
                       )
                     ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map,
                       )
    ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate,
                       )
    ) |>
  # Add natural spline with 3 knots (4 df) for neq
  step_spline_natural(neq, deg_free = 4)

avp_m1_lr_preproc <- list(
  avp_m1_main = avp_m1_lr_rec_main, 
  avp_m1_ns = avp_m1_lr_rec_ns
  )

avp_m1_lr_models <- 
  workflow_set(avp_m1_lr_preproc,
               list(logistic = logistic_reg(engine = "glm")), 
               cross = FALSE)
```

Determine performance metrics (AUCROC and Brier score) using cross-validation resampling. These metrics were selected based on recommendations in [Van Calster 2025](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landig.2025.100916), First, declare the survival metrics. Second, establish the cross-validation folds. Will use 10-fold cross-validation with 5 repeats, stratified by event. Third, save the predictions in order to visualize the model fit and residuals. Fourth, fit the model to the resampled dataset. Lastly, collect the predictions.

Resample each model in the workflow set (`avp_m1_lr_models`).

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(avp, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

avp_m1_lr_models_fit <- 
  avp_m1_lr_models |>
  workflow_map("fit_resamples", seed = 2026, verbose = TRUE,
               resamples = train_cv, metrics = class_metrics,
               control = keep_pred
               )
avp_m1_lr_preds <- 
  collect_predictions(avp_m1_lr_models_fit, summarize = FALSE)
```

Collect then show the metrics (summarized over all cross-validation folds).

```{r}
avp_m1_lr_mets <- 
  collect_metrics(avp_m1_lr_models_fit) |>
  # Compute 95% Wald CIs across the 50 resamples
  mutate(
    conf.low.95 = mean - qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    conf.high.95 = mean + qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    mean_ci = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
  ) |>
  select(wflow_id, .metric, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95, mean_ci) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = c(mean_ci, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
    )

avp_m1_lr_mets |>
  select(wflow_id, mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Vasopressin m1 (Logistic Regression) Metric Comparison",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats). Presented as mean (95% CI)."
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    mean_ci_roc_auc = "AUROC",
    mean_ci_brier_class = "Brier Score",
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class)
    )
```

The model with non-linear terms (`avp_m1_ns_logistic`) had better than the main effects model (`avp_m1_main_logistic`). 

Show a non-stylized plot (autoplot) of the AUROC comparison.

```{r}
avp_m1_lr_preds |>
  group_by(wflow_id) |>
  roc_curve(response, .pred_Response) |>
  autoplot()
```

The plot shows the ROC curve is consistently higher with the model incorporating the spline term compared with the model with main effects only.

### Machine Learning

#### Regularized (Elastic Net) {#sec-avp-m1-glmnet}

Fit regularized (elastic net) models. Use essentially the same recipes as for the logistic regression models (main effects and spline term for `neq`) except dummy code nominal predictors and normalize (center and scale) continuous predictors (normalization is done automatically by `glmnet` but this makes the step explicit).

```{r}
avp_m2_rec_main <- avp_m1_lr_rec_main |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

avp_m2_rec_ns <- avp_m1_lr_rec_ns |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

avp_m2_glmnet_preproc <- list(
  avp_m2_main = avp_m2_rec_main, 
  avp_m2_ns = avp_m2_rec_ns
  )

avp_m2_glmnet_models <- 
  workflow_set(avp_m2_glmnet_preproc,
               list(glmnet = logistic_reg(
                 engine = "glmnet",
                 mode = "classification",
                 penalty = tune(),     # lambda
                 mixture = tune()      # alpha
                 )),
               cross = TRUE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(avp, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

pen_grid <- grid_space_filling(
  penalty(range = c(-5, 0)), # log10 scale, reasonable range for elastic net
  mixture(range = c(0, 1)),  # default
  size = 30
  )

avp_m2_glmnet_models_fit <- 
  avp_m2_glmnet_models |> 
  workflow_map("tune_grid", seed = 2026, verbose = TRUE,
               resamples = train_cv, grid = pen_grid,
               metrics = class_metrics, control = keep_pred
               )

workflow_ids <- avp_m2_glmnet_models_fit$wflow_id

# Loop over workflows to finalize, fit, and collect results
avp_m2_glmnet_final_fit <- map(workflow_ids, function(wf_id) {
  
  # Extract tuning results for this workflow
  wf_result <- extract_workflow_set_result(avp_m2_glmnet_models_fit, id = wf_id)
  
  # Get best parameters by AUROC
  best_params <- select_best(wf_result, metric = "roc_auc")
  
  # Extract the workflow object itself
  wf <- extract_workflow(avp_m2_glmnet_models_fit, id = wf_id)
  
  # Finalize the workflow with best hyperparameters
  final_wf <- finalize_workflow(
    wf,
    best_params
  )
  
  # Fit the final workflow to the training set
  final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = avp)
  
  # Collect resampling metrics for this workflow from tuning
  cv_metrics <- collect_metrics(wf_result) |>
    filter(penalty == best_params$penalty,
           mixture == best_params$mixture)
  
  # Collect predictions for the best parameters
  cv_preds <- collect_predictions(wf_result, summarize = TRUE) |>
    filter(penalty == best_params$penalty,
           mixture == best_params$mixture)
  
  # Return as a list
  list(
    workflow_id = wf_id,
    best_params = best_params,
    final_workflow = final_wf,
    final_fit = final_fit,
    cv_metrics = cv_metrics,
    cv_predictions = cv_preds
  )
})

# Name the list elements by workflow
names(avp_m2_glmnet_final_fit) <- workflow_ids
rm(workflow_ids)
```

Show elastic net hyperparameters resulting in the best fit.

```{r}
imap_dfr(avp_m2_glmnet_final_fit, 
         ~ .x$best_params |> mutate(wflow_id = .y)
         ) |>
  select(wflow_id, penalty, mixture) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Vasopressin m2 Elastic Net Best Hyperparameters",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats)"
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    penalty = "Penalty (lambda [λ])",
    mixture = "Mixture (alpha [α])"
    ) |>
  fmt_number(decimals = 4) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(penalty, mixture)
    )
```

These parameters suggest that applying a small penalty term (lambda) to the main effects model helps a little and it is essentially a LASSO situation with mixture 0.9. For the spline model there is no meaningful penalty and the elastic net model is very close to the unpenalized logistic regression model.

Collect metrics and display table (comparing to the logistic regression model fits).

```{r}
avp_m2_glmnet_mets <- 
 avp_m2_glmnet_final_fit |> map(function(x) {
    x$cv_metrics |>
    mutate(wflow_id = x$workflow_id)
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(
    conf.low.95 = mean - qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    conf.high.95 = mean + qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    mean_ci = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
  ) |>
  select(wflow_id, .metric, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95, mean_ci) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = c(mean_ci, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
    )

bind_rows(avp_m1_lr_mets, avp_m2_glmnet_mets)  |>
  select(wflow_id, mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Vasopressin m2 (Elastic Net) Metric Comparison",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats). Presented as mean (95% CI)."
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    mean_ci_roc_auc = "AUROC",
    mean_ci_brier_class = "Brier Score",
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class)
    )
```

The metrics are essentially the same without and with regularization. This suggests that the model is not materially overfit. And in both models the spline term for `neq` improves fit.

#### Random Forest

Fit a random forest model with the "ranger" engine.

```{r}
#| message: FALSE

avp_m3_rf_rec <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = avp) |>
  # Declare age, sex, and race_eth in a bystander role to keep it in the 
  # resampling dataset for future use in fairness checks
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  # Single (linear regression) imputation for missing quantitative predictors
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h
                       )
                     ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map
                       )
    ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate
                       )
    )

avp_m3_rf_preproc <- list(avp_m3_rf = avp_m3_rf_rec)

avp_m3_rf_models <- 
  workflow_set(avp_m3_rf_preproc,
               list(ranger = rand_forest(
                 engine = "ranger",
                 mode = "classification",
                 trees = 1000,      # Default is 500, 1000 is better      
                 mtry = tune(),     # Number of randomly selected predictors     
                 min_n = tune()     # Minimum node size   
                 )),
               cross = TRUE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(avp, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

# Prep recipe and determine predictor count
avp_m3_rf_rec_prep <- prep(avp_m3_rf_rec)

x_train <- bake(avp_m3_rf_rec_prep, new_data = NULL) |>
  select(-c(response, age, sex, race_eth))

p <- ncol(x_train) # p == 10

rf_param_set <- parameters(
  mtry(range = c(1L, 10L)), #sqrt(p) ~= 3, (p / 2) == 5, which is too narrow
  min_n(range = c(2L, 50L))
)

initial_candidates <- grid_space_filling(
  rf_param_set,
  size = 30
)

race_ctrl <- control_race(
  save_pred = TRUE,
  save_workflow = TRUE,
  parallel_over = "resamples",
  verbose = FALSE
)

avp_m3_rf_model_fit <-
  avp_m3_rf_models |>
  workflow_map(
    "tune_race_anova", seed = 2026, resamples = train_cv,
    grid = initial_candidates, metrics = class_metrics, control = race_ctrl
  )

# Get workflow IDs
workflow_ids <- avp_m3_rf_model_fit$wflow_id

# Finalize, fit, and collect results for the workflow
avp_m3_rf_final_fit <- map(workflow_ids, function(wf_id) {
  # Extract tuning (race) results for this workflow
  wf_result <- extract_workflow_set_result(
    avp_m3_rf_model_fit,
    id = wf_id
    )
  # Select best hyperparameters by AUROC
  best_params <- select_best(wf_result, metric = "roc_auc")
  # Extract the workflow itself
  wf <- extract_workflow(avp_m3_rf_model_fit, id = wf_id)
  # Finalize workflow with best hyperparameters
  final_wf <- finalize_workflow(wf, best_params)
  # Fit finalized workflow to derivation data
  final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = avp)
  # Collect CV metrics for the selected configuration
  cv_metrics <- collect_metrics(wf_result) |>
    filter(.config == best_params$.config)
  # Collect CV predictions for the selected configuration
  cv_predictions <- collect_predictions(wf_result) |>
    filter(.config == best_params$.config)
  # Return results
  list(
    workflow_id     = wf_id,
    best_params     = best_params,
    final_workflow  = final_wf,
    final_fit       = final_fit,
    cv_metrics      = cv_metrics,
    cv_predictions  = cv_predictions
    )
})

names(avp_m3_rf_final_fit) <- map_chr(avp_m3_rf_final_fit, "workflow_id")
```

Show hyperparameters resulting in the best fit.

```{r}
imap_dfr(avp_m3_rf_final_fit, 
         ~ .x$best_params |> mutate(workflow_id = .y)
         ) |>
  select(workflow_id, mtry, min_n) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Random Forest Best Hyperparameters",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats)"
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    workflow_id = "Model",
    mtry = "Random Variables at Split (mtry)",
    min_n = "Min Terminal Node Size (min_n)"
    ) |>
  fmt_number(decimals = 0) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(workflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(mtry, min_n)
    )
```

These parameters show that in the best performing model at each split the forest considers only one randomly chosen predictor. This is "maximum decorrelation" among trees. Because CV chose mtry == 1, it suggest no single predictor is substantially dominant and that the ensemble benefits from forcing trees to explore different predictors. The selection of min_n = 25 indicates that the forest prefers a moderate amount of smoothing to represent non-linear effects, but following small local patterns (with lower min_n) is not useful.

Generate a boosted tree model with the "xgboost" engine in {tidymodels}.

```{r}
avp_m4_xgb_rec <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = avp) |>
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(

      criteria_met, sofa2_no_cv,
      neq, shock_dur_h
    )
  ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(
      heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era,
      criteria_met, sofa2_no_cv,
      neq, shock_dur_h, map
    )
  ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(
      heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era,
      criteria_met, sofa2_no_cv,
      neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate
    )
  ) |>
  # Dummy code nominal predictors
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

  workflow_set(avp_m4_xgb_preproc,
               list(xgboost = boost_tree(
                 trees = 1000,              # Number of trees
```

The largest performance gain came from modeling `neq` with a natural spline (`avp_m1_ns_logistic`) instead of main effects alone (`avp_m1_main_logistic`). The differences between the spline logistic regression model and machine learning models are very minor (\<=0.01 difference for each metric point estimate) and they generally have similarly modest performance.

Considering the goal of future model implementation in the electronic medical record and explainability to clinicians, a logistic regression model (`avp_m1_ns_logistic`) is preferred. The XGBoost model (`avp_m4_boost_xgboost`) had marginally better performance, though. These two models will be carried forward for calibration assessment prior to final model selection.

### Calibration {#sec-avp-cal}

Use the `pmcalibration()` function from the `{pmcalibration}` package to assess calibration (vignette [here](https://stephenrho.github.io/pmcalibration/)).
Calibration will be assessed using pooled out-of-fold predictions from repeated 10-fold cross-validation. For each participant, predicted probabilities will be averaged across the five cross-validation repeats and compared with observed outcomes using flexible calibration curves from `pmcalibration()`. The `pmcalibration()` function estimates group‑wise calibration using restricted cubic splines, with explicit handling of censoring via Kaplan–Meier–type estimators, and adds bootstrap uncertainty (1000 replications) around the calibration curve. Curves will be generated using a restricted cubic splines smoother with 3 knots; the `{pmcalibration}` package default is 5 knots for the restricted cubic splines smoother, but [Austin 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32548928/) found that 3 knots led to less bias. Notably, the `{pmcalibration}` package assesses "moderate" calibration via non-linear calibration curves as described in [Van Calster 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26772608/). 

#### Logistic Regression Model

Compare the observed outcomes from the original derivation dataset with the predicted probabilities for the outcome generated in the out-of-fold predictions from the repeated cross-validation process (averaging the out-of-fold predictions for each patient).

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 6

avp_m1_lr_preds_cv <- avp_m1_lr_preds |>
  filter(wflow_id == "avp_m1_ns_logistic") |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    response = first(response),
    .pred_Response = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    response_num = if_else(response == "Response", 1, 0)
  )

set.seed(2026)
avp_lr_cal <-
  pmcalibration(
    y = avp_m1_lr_preds_cv$response_num,
    p = avp_m1_lr_preds_cv$.pred_Response,
    ci = "boot", # n = 1000 replicates is the default
    smooth = "rcs",
    nk = 3 # 5 knots is default, 3 has less bias
    )

invisible(pdf("avp_logistic_calibration.pdf"))
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), 
    cex.axis = 1.4, cex.lab = 1.8, cex.main = 2,
    mar = c(5.1, 5.5, 1.4, 1.6), # bottom, left, top, right
    mgp = c(3.5, 1, 0)
    )
plot(avp_lr_cal)
invisible(dev.off())
```

The cross-validated predictions from the logistic regression model with a natural spline term for `neq` are very well calibrated relative to the observed outcomes in the derivation cohort.

Although the discrimination (AUROC) for the logistic regression model (with a spline term) was only modest, the calibration is very good. This means the probabilities the model produces are very trustworthy.

#### XGBoost Model

Use the same calibration assessment workflow for the boosted trees (XGBoost) model.

```{r}
  summarise(
    response = first(response),
    .pred_Response = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"

    response_num = if_else(response == "Response", 1, 0)
```

#### Quantitative metrics

Generate and display metrics for the two models. The "Eavg" is the same as "integrated calibration index" (ICI), therefore will make this clarification in the output. The "ECI" is the average squared difference between predicted and observed probabilities (multiplied by 100). For each of the calibration metrics outlined, lower values are better.

```{r}
# Display the table
(avp_cal_metrics_tbl <-
  bind_rows(
    as_tibble(avp_lr_cal$metrics, rownames = "metric") |>
      mutate(model = "Logistic (spline)"),
    as_tibble(avp_xgb_cal$metrics, rownames = "metric") |>
      mutate(model = "XGBoost")
  ) |>
  select(model, metric, value) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = metric,
    values_from = value
  ) |>
  rename(
    Model = model,
    `Eavg (ICI)` = Eavg
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Vasopressin Model Calibration Metrics"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(`Eavg (ICI)`, E50, E90, Emax, ECI),
    decimals = 4
  ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center"
  ))
```

Both models are extremely well calibrated. The XGBoost model has consistently better quantitative calibration metrics, but the differences between models are very small.

### Decision Curve Analysis

To assess if there may be clinical utility with the two vasopressin response prediction models under consideration, perform a decision curve analysis (DCA). To correct for overfitting, use the out-of-fold predictions for each model.

First, extract predictions from the logistic regression and XGBoost models, and combine.

```{r}
# Extract the out-of-fold predictions for each model
# Then average predictions across the 5 CV repeats using .row
# Logistic model
avp_lr_dca <- avp_m1_lr_preds |>
  filter(wflow_id == "avp_m1_ns_logistic") |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    response = first(response),
    p_logistic = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# XGBoost model
avp_xgb_dca <- avp_m4_xgb_final_fit[[1]]$cv_predictions |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    p_xgb = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Combine
avp_dca_data <- avp_lr_dca |>
  left_join(avp_xgb_dca, by = ".row")
```

Then run DCA and plot.

```{r avp-dca}
#| warning: false

avp_dca <- dca(
  response == "Response" ~ p_logistic + p_xgb,
  data = avp_dca_data
  )

(avp_dca_plot <- 
  ggplot(as_tibble(avp_dca) |>
           filter(net_benefit >= -0.006 &
                    net_benefit <= 0.31 &
                    threshold <=0.71
                  ) |>
           mutate(label = fct_relevel(label, "Treat None", "Treat All",
                                     "p_logistic", "p_xgb"
                                     )),
         aes(x = threshold,
             y = net_benefit,
             color = label,
             group = label)) +
    geom_smooth(method = loess, formula = y ~ x,
                linewidth = 1, se = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
      "p_logistic" = "#0072B2",
      "p_xgb" = "#7876B1FF",
      "Treat All" = "#009E73",
      "Treat None" = "#D55E00"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "p_logistic" = "Logistic regression",
        "p_xgb" = "XGBoost",
        "Treat All" = "Treat all",
        "Treat None" = "Treat none"
      )) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(-0.006, 0.31),
      expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0))
      ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0.1, 0.71),
      breaks = seq(0, 0.7, by = 0.1),
      expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0.02))
      ) +
    labs(
      title = "Vasopressin Model Comparison",
      x = "Probability Threshold",
      y = "Net Benefit",
      color = NULL
      ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.52, y = 0.06, label = "Logistic model",
             color = "#0072B2", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.62, y = 0.03, label = "XGBoost model",
             color = "#7876B1FF", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.23, y = 0.07, label = "Treat all",
             color = "#009E73", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.16, y = 0.01, label = "Treat none",
             color = "#D55E00", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(family = "sans"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      axis.line.x = element_line(),
      axis.line.y = element_line(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_line(),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm")
    ))
```

Both models are better than "Treat none" and "Treat all" from probability thresholds about 0.1 to about 0.6. The two models have essentially the same net benefit at probability thresholds below 0.5, with the XGBoost model having slightly higher net benefit at probability thresholds from 0.5 to 0.65.

Obtain exact threshold values for positive net benefit with logistic regression and XGBoost models. To improve matching with visualization in the figure, use a practical tolerance value of 0.001 for the thresholds.

```{r}
as_tibble(avp_dca) |>
  select(threshold, label, net_benefit) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = label, values_from = net_benefit) |>
  filter(!is.na(p_logistic), !is.na(p_xgb), 
         !is.na(`Treat All`), !is.na(`Treat None`)
         ) |>
  summarise(
    min_prob_thresh_lr = min(threshold[p_logistic > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_logistic > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             ),
    max_prob_thresh_lr = max(threshold[p_logistic > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_logistic > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             ),
    min_prob_thresh_xgb = min(threshold[p_xgb > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_xgb > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             ),
    max_prob_thresh_xgb = max(threshold[p_xgb > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_xgb > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             )
  )
```

The vasopressin response logistic regression model had higher net benefit than the "Treat all" and "Treat none" curves at threshold probabilities from 0.08 to 0.61. The vasopressin response XGBoost model had higher net benefit than the "Treat all" and "Treat none" curves at threshold probabilities from 0.08 to 0.68.

### Model Selection

Overall, compared with the logistic regression model with a spline term for `neq`, the XGBoost model demonstrated slightly better discrimination, overall performance, calibration, and net benefit on decision curve analysis. However, the magnitude of improvement was very small. Considering overall performance similarity but higher interpretability and implementation readiness for a logistic regression model, the logistic regression model with a spline term for norepinephrine dose (`avp_m1_ns_logistic`) was selected as the final model for vasopressin.

#### Refit to Whole Derivation Dataset

Refit the final model (`avp_m1_ns_logistic`) in the whole vasopressin derivation dataset (`avp`).

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
avp_mod_final_wf <- extract_workflow(
  avp_m1_lr_models,
  id = "avp_m1_ns_logistic"
  )
avp_mod_final_fit_dev <- fit(avp_mod_final_wf, avp)
```

Extract engine data and estimate apparent performance on derivation data.

```{r}
avp_lr_fit <- extract_fit_engine(avp_mod_final_fit_dev)
avp_apparent_performance <- glance(avp_lr_fit) |> 
  transmute(
    nobs,
    n_parameters = length(coef(avp_lr_fit)) - 1,
    r2_nag = performance::r2_nagelkerke(avp_lr_fit)
  )

## Prepare data 
avp_rec_trained <- extract_recipe(avp_mod_final_fit_dev)

avp_baked_dev <- bake(
  avp_rec_trained,
  new_data = avp,
  all_predictors()
)

avp_dev_score_data <- bind_cols(
  avp |> select(response),
  avp_baked_dev
)

# Generate metrics
avp_dev_score <- 
  Score(
    object = list(avp_lr_fit),
    formula = response ~ 1,
    data = avp_dev_score_data,
    metrics = c("auc", "brier")
    )

# Extract and format results
auc_ci <-
  avp_dev_score$AUC$score |>
  as_tibble() |>
  transmute(
    auc = as.numeric(AUC),
    auc_lower = as.numeric(lower),
    auc_upper = as.numeric(upper)
  )

brier_ci <-
  avp_dev_score$Brier$score |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(model == "glm") |>
  transmute(
    brier = as.numeric(Brier),
    brier_lower = as.numeric(lower),
    brier_upper = as.numeric(upper)
  )

avp_dev_mets <- cbind(auc_ci, brier_ci) |>
  mutate(
    AUROC = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", auc, auc_lower, auc_upper),
    Brier = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", brier, brier_lower, brier_upper)
  )
rm(auc_ci, brier_ci)

cbind(avp_apparent_performance, 
      avp_dev_mets |> select(AUROC, Brier)) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(r2_nag), 
             decimals = 3
             ) |>
  tab_header(title = "Vasopressin Logistic Regression Model Fit and Apparent Performance Parameters",
             subtitle = "In Derivation (Ohio) Dataset") |>
  cols_label(
    nobs = "N",
    n_parameters =  "Parameters (n)",
    r2_nag = "R2 (Nagelkerke)",
    Brier = "Brier Score"
    ) |>
  cols_align(align = "center")
```

Show model parameters.

```{r}
(avp_lr_param_estimates <- 
   tidy(avp_lr_fit,
        conf.int = TRUE
        ) |>
   # Since the model predicts the second factor level ("No Response") for 
   # yardstick() ease, invert the coefficients to express ORs for "Response"
   # Use a higher number of reported digits for some parameters
   mutate(estimate_ci = case_when(
     term == "(Intercept)" ~ sprintf("%.9f (%.9f, %.9f)",
                                    exp(-estimate),
                                    exp(-conf.high),
                                    exp(-conf.low)

     .default = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)",
                        exp(-estimate),
                        exp(-conf.high),

   gt() |>

     estimate_ci = "Response Odds Ratio (95% CI)"
     ) |>
   cols_align(align = "left", columns = term) |>
   cols_align(align = "center", columns = estimate_ci))
```

#### Compare to Simple Model

Compare the selected multivariable model (`avp_m1_ns_logistic`) with a simple model that only includes `neq` with a spline term.

```{r}
lr_spec <- 
  logistic_reg() |>
  set_engine("glm")

avp_m0_lr_rec_ns <-
  recipe(response ~ neq, data = avp) |>
  step_spline_natural(neq, deg_free = 5)

avp_m0_lr_preproc <- list(avp_m0_neq_only = avp_m0_lr_rec_ns,
                          avp_m1_multivar = avp_m1_lr_rec_ns
                          )

avp_m0_lr_model <- 
  workflow_set(avp_m0_lr_preproc,
               list(logistic = logistic_reg(engine = "glm")), 
               cross = FALSE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(avp, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

avp_m0_lr_model_fit <- 
  avp_m0_lr_model |>
  workflow_map("fit_resamples", seed = 2026, verbose = TRUE,
               resamples = train_cv, metrics = class_metrics,
               control = keep_pred
               )
avp_m0_lr_preds <- 
  collect_predictions(avp_m0_lr_model_fit, summarize = FALSE)

avp_m0_lr_mets <- 
  collect_metrics(avp_m0_lr_model_fit) |>
  # Compute 95% Wald CIs across the 50 resamples
  mutate(
    conf.low.95 = mean - qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    conf.high.95 = mean + qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    mean_ci = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
  ) |>
  select(wflow_id, .metric, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95, mean_ci) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = c(mean_ci, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
    )

avp_m0_lr_mets |>
  select(wflow_id, mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Vasopressin Final Model Performance vs. NE Alone",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats). Presented as mean (95% CI)."
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    mean_ci_roc_auc = "AUROC",
    mean_ci_brier_class = "Brier Score",
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class)
    )
```

The multivariable model has substantially better metrics than the simple model using `neq` alone. Using additional patient information beyond relying on norepinephrine dose alone provides meaningful improvement in the prediction of vasopressin response.

Show a non-stylized plot (autoplot) of the AUROC comparison.

```{r}
avp_m0_lr_preds |>
  group_by(wflow_id) |>
  roc_curve(response, .pred_Response) |>
  autoplot()
```

The ROC curves are separated across essentially the entire plot range, with the multivariable model showing consistently better predictive discrimination than the univariable model only including norepinephrine dose (with a spline term).

Potential interpretation for manuscript: "Although norepinephrine dose is commonly used to estimate the likelihood of vasopressin response, a model based on norepinephrine dose alone demonstrated substantially lower discrimination (AUROC 0.636) and worse overall predictive performance (Brier score 0.214) than the multivariable model (AUROC 0.700, Brier score 0.202)."

## Epinephrine

This section will build and evaluate prediction models for response after initiation of epinephrine as the first adjunctive vasopressor. The same approaches as for vasopressin models will be used here with less annotation. For more annotation regarding the rationale for model building and evaluation steps see @sec-avp.

### Logistic Regression

Here, use logistic regression to generate prediction models using two approaches: 1) main effects (additive) only, and 2) non-linear effects of predictors.

The two models will be built in one `workflow_set()`. First, generate a Spearman's $\rho^2$ rank correlation plot to assess for potential predictor transformation (non-linear effects).

```{r}
plot(spearman2(response ~ ., data = epi |> select(-c(age, sex, race_eth))))

invisible(pdf("epi_spearman.pdf"))
plot(spearman2(response ~ ., data = epi |> select(-c(age, sex, race_eth))),
     main = ""
     )
title(main = expression("Epinephrine Spearman " * rho^2))
invisible(dev.off())
```

The Spearman's $\rho^2$ rank correlation plot shows that `map` has the highest potential to improve model fit with a non-linear transformation. Because this is a quantitative variable, introduce a natural spline with 3 knots (4 df) to spend all of the available degrees of freedom (12 df in the main effects model and 15 total available). Notably, all of the predictors have a relatively low $\rho^2$ value, therefore the non-linear model is not expected to substantially improve fit.

As noted in @sec-miss-oh, there are missing data in the same three variables as for vasopressin. Therefore, the same imputation approach will be used.

```{r}
# Main effects recipe
epi_m1_lr_rec_main <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = epi) |>
  # Declare age, sex, and race_eth in a bystander role to keep it in the 
  # resampling dataset for future use in fairness checks
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  # Single (linear regression) imputation for missing quantitatitve predictors
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h
                       )
                     ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map
                       )
    ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate
                       )
    )

# Non-linear effects recipe
epi_m1_lr_rec_ns <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = epi) |>
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, 
                       )
                     ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map,
                       )
    ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate,
                       )
    ) |>
  # Add natural spline with 3 knots (4 df) for map
  step_spline_natural(map, deg_free = 4)

# Set up pre-processing and model workflow_set()
epi_m1_lr_preproc <- list(
  epi_m1_main = epi_m1_lr_rec_main, 
  epi_m1_ns = epi_m1_lr_rec_ns
  )

epi_m1_lr_models <- 
  workflow_set(epi_m1_lr_preproc,
               list(logistic = logistic_reg(engine = "glm")), 
               cross = FALSE)

# Resample each model in the set with 10-fold CV (5 repeats)
set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(epi, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

epi_m1_lr_models_fit <- 
  epi_m1_lr_models |>
  workflow_map("fit_resamples", seed = 2026, verbose = TRUE,
               resamples = train_cv, metrics = class_metrics,
               control = keep_pred
               )

# Collect predictions
epi_m1_lr_preds <- 
  collect_predictions(epi_m1_lr_models_fit, summarize = FALSE)

# Collect then show the metrics
epi_m1_lr_mets <- 
  collect_metrics(epi_m1_lr_models_fit) |>
  mutate(
    conf.low.95 = mean - qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    conf.high.95 = mean + qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    mean_ci = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
  ) |>
  select(wflow_id, .metric, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95, mean_ci) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = c(mean_ci, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
    )

epi_m1_lr_mets |>
  select(wflow_id, mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Epinephrine m1 (Logistic Regression) Metric Comparison",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats). Presented as mean (95% CI)."
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    mean_ci_roc_auc = "AUROC",
    mean_ci_brier_class = "Brier Score",
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class)
    )
```

The two logistic regression modeling approaches had essentially the same discrimination (AUROC) and overall performance (Brier score). The performance of both models was better than chance but not impressive.

```{r}
epi_m1_lr_preds |>
  group_by(wflow_id) |>
  roc_curve(response, .pred_Response) |>
  autoplot()
```

The two curves have a lot of overlap. The non-linear (spline) model is slightly better at lower values and the main effects model is slightly better at higher values.

### Machine Learning

#### Regularized (Elastic Net)

Fit regularized (elastic net) models.

```{r}
epi_m2_rec_main <- epi_m1_lr_rec_main |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

epi_m2_rec_ns <- epi_m1_lr_rec_ns |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

epi_m2_glmnet_preproc <- list(
  epi_m2_main = epi_m2_rec_main, 
  epi_m2_ns = epi_m2_rec_ns
  )

epi_m2_glmnet_models <- 
  workflow_set(epi_m2_glmnet_preproc,
               list(glmnet = logistic_reg(
                 engine = "glmnet",
                 mode = "classification",
                 penalty = tune(),     # lambda
                 mixture = tune()      # alpha
                 )),
               cross = TRUE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(epi, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

pen_grid <- grid_space_filling(
  penalty(range = c(-5, 0)), # log10 scale, reasonable range for elastic net
  mixture(range = c(0, 1)),  # default
  size = 30
  )

epi_m2_glmnet_models_fit <- 
  epi_m2_glmnet_models |> 
  workflow_map("tune_grid", seed = 2026, verbose = TRUE,
               resamples = train_cv, grid = pen_grid,
               metrics = class_metrics, control = keep_pred
               )

workflow_ids <- epi_m2_glmnet_models_fit$wflow_id

# Loop over workflows to finalize, fit, and collect results
epi_m2_glmnet_final_fit <- map(workflow_ids, function(wf_id) {
  
  # Extract tuning results for this workflow
  wf_result <- extract_workflow_set_result(epi_m2_glmnet_models_fit, id = wf_id)
  
  # Get best parameters by AUROC
  best_params <- select_best(wf_result, metric = "roc_auc")
  
  # Extract the workflow object itself
  wf <- extract_workflow(epi_m2_glmnet_models_fit, id = wf_id)
  
  # Finalize the workflow with best hyperparameters
  final_wf <- finalize_workflow(
    wf,
    best_params
  )
  
  # Fit the final workflow to the training set
  final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = epi)
  
  # Collect resampling metrics for this workflow from tuning
  cv_metrics <- collect_metrics(wf_result) |>
    filter(penalty == best_params$penalty,
           mixture == best_params$mixture)
  
  # Collect predictions for the best parameters
  cv_preds <- collect_predictions(wf_result, summarize = TRUE) |>
    filter(penalty == best_params$penalty,
           mixture == best_params$mixture)
  
  # Return as a list
  list(
    workflow_id = wf_id,
    best_params = best_params,
    final_workflow = final_wf,
    final_fit = final_fit,
    cv_metrics = cv_metrics,
    cv_predictions = cv_preds
  )
})

# Name the list elements by workflow
names(epi_m2_glmnet_final_fit) <- workflow_ids
rm(workflow_ids)
```

Show elastic net hyperparameters resulting in the best fit.

```{r}
imap_dfr(epi_m2_glmnet_final_fit, 
         ~ .x$best_params |> mutate(wflow_id = .y)
         ) |>
  select(wflow_id, penalty, mixture) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Epinephrine m2 Elastic Net Best Hyperparameters",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats)"
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    penalty = "Penalty (lambda [λ])",
    mixture = "Mixture (alpha [α])"
    ) |>
  fmt_number(decimals = 4) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(penalty, mixture)
    )
```

Collect metrics and display table (comparing to the logistic regression model fits).

```{r}

 epi_m2_glmnet_final_fit |> map(function(x) {
    x$cv_metrics |>
    mutate(wflow_id = x$workflow_id)
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(
    conf.low.95 = mean - qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    conf.high.95 = mean + qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    mean_ci = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
  ) |>
  select(wflow_id, .metric, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95, mean_ci) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = c(mean_ci, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
    )

bind_rows(epi_m1_lr_mets, epi_m2_glmnet_mets)  |>
  select(wflow_id, mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Epinephrine m2 (Elastic Net) Metric Comparison",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats). Presented as mean (95% CI)."
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    mean_ci_roc_auc = "AUROC",
    mean_ci_brier_class = "Brier Score",
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class)
    )
```

The regularized (elastic net) models performed slightly better than the logistic regression models.

#### Random Forest

Fit a random forest model.

```{r}
epi_m3_rf_rec <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = epi) |>
  # Declare age, sex, and race_eth in a bystander role to keep it in the 
  # resampling dataset for future use in fairness checks
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  # Single (linear regression) imputation for missing quantitative predictors
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h
                       )
                     ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map
                       )
    ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate
                       )
    )

epi_m3_rf_preproc <- list(epi_m3_rf = epi_m3_rf_rec)

epi_m3_rf_models <- 
  workflow_set(epi_m3_rf_preproc,
               list(ranger = rand_forest(
                 engine = "ranger",
                 mode = "classification",
                 trees = 1000,      # Default is 500, 1000 is better      
                 mtry = tune(),     # Number of randomly selected predictors     
                 min_n = tune()     # Minimum node size   
                 )),
               cross = TRUE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(epi, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

# Prep recipe and determine predictor count
epi_m3_rf_rec_prep <- prep(epi_m3_rf_rec)

x_train <- bake(epi_m3_rf_rec_prep, new_data = NULL) |>
  select(-c(response, age, sex, race_eth))

p <- ncol(x_train) # p == 10

rf_param_set <- parameters(
  mtry(range = c(1L, 10L)), #sqrt(p) ~= 3, (p / 2) == 5, which is too narrow
  min_n(range = c(2L, 50L))
)

initial_candidates <- grid_space_filling(
  rf_param_set,
  size = 30
)

race_ctrl <- control_race(
  save_pred = TRUE,
  save_workflow = TRUE,
  parallel_over = "resamples",
  verbose = FALSE
)

epi_m3_rf_model_fit <-
  epi_m3_rf_models |>
  workflow_map(
    "tune_race_anova", seed = 2026, resamples = train_cv,
    grid = initial_candidates, metrics = class_metrics, control = race_ctrl
  )

# Get workflow IDs
workflow_ids <- epi_m3_rf_model_fit$wflow_id

# Finalize, fit, and collect results for the workflow
epi_m3_rf_final_fit <- map(workflow_ids, function(wf_id) {
  # Extract tuning (race) results for this workflow
  wf_result <- extract_workflow_set_result(
    epi_m3_rf_model_fit,
    id = wf_id
    )
  # Select best hyperparameters by AUROC
  best_params <- select_best(wf_result, metric = "roc_auc")
  # Extract the workflow itself
  wf <- extract_workflow(epi_m3_rf_model_fit, id = wf_id)
  # Finalize workflow with best hyperparameters
  final_wf <- finalize_workflow(wf, best_params)
  # Fit finalized workflow to derivation data
  final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = epi)
  # Collect CV metrics for the selected configuration
  cv_metrics <- collect_metrics(wf_result) |>
    filter(.config == best_params$.config)
  # Collect CV predictions for the selected configuration
  cv_predictions <- collect_predictions(wf_result) |>
    filter(.config == best_params$.config)
  # Return results
  list(
    workflow_id     = wf_id,
    best_params     = best_params,
    final_workflow  = final_wf,
    final_fit       = final_fit,
    cv_metrics      = cv_metrics,
    cv_predictions  = cv_predictions
    )
})

names(epi_m3_rf_final_fit) <- map_chr(epi_m3_rf_final_fit, "workflow_id")
```

#### Boosted Trees

Generate a boosted tree model.

```{r}
epi_m4_xgb_rec <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = epi) |>
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(
      heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era,
      criteria_met, sofa2_no_cv,
      neq, shock_dur_h
    )
  ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(
      heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era,
      criteria_met, sofa2_no_cv,
      neq, shock_dur_h, map
    )
  ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(
      heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era,
      criteria_met, sofa2_no_cv,
      neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate
    )
  ) |>
  # Dummy code nominal predictors
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

epi_m4_xgb_preproc <- list(epi_m4_boost = epi_m4_xgb_rec)

epi_m4_xgb_model <- 
  workflow_set(epi_m4_xgb_preproc,
               list(xgboost = boost_tree(
                 trees = 1000,              # Number of trees       
                 tree_depth = tune(),       # Tree depth: # of "interactions" 
                 min_n = tune(),            # Minimum node size
                 loss_reduction = tune(),   # Reduction in the loss function required to split further
                 sample_size = tune(),      # Proportion of data exposed to fitting routine
                 mtry = tune(),             # Random predictors at each split
                 learn_rate = tune()        # Rate at which the boosting algorithm adapts
                 ) |>
                   set_engine("xgboost") |>  
                   set_mode("classification")
                 ),
               cross = FALSE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(epi, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

# Prep recipe and determine post-dummy predictor count
epi_m4_xgb_rec_prep <- prep(epi_m4_xgb_rec)

x_train <- bake(epi_m4_xgb_rec_prep, new_data = NULL) |>
  select(-c(response, age, sex, race_eth))

p <- ncol(x_train) # p == 10

# Select parameters (particularly depth) based p==10 and RF optimal parameters
xgb_params <- parameters(
  tree_depth(range = c(1L, 6L)),
  min_n(range = c(2L, 50L)),
  learn_rate(range = c(-3, -0.5)),
  loss_reduction(),
  sample_prop(range = c(0.5, 1.0)),
  finalize(mtry(), x_train)
  )

initial_candidates <- grid_space_filling(
  xgb_params,
  size = 30
  )

race_ctrl <- control_race(
  save_pred = TRUE,
  save_workflow = TRUE,
  parallel_over = "resamples",
  verbose = FALSE
  )

epi_m4_xgb_model_fit <-
  epi_m4_xgb_model |>
  workflow_map(
    "tune_race_anova",
    seed = 2026,
    resamples = train_cv,
    grid = initial_candidates,
    metrics = class_metrics,
    control = race_ctrl
    )

workflow_ids <- epi_m4_xgb_model_fit$wflow_id

# Finalize, fit, and collect results the workflow
epi_m4_xgb_final_fit <- map(workflow_ids, function(wf_id) {
  # Extract tuning (race) results for this workflow
  wf_result <- extract_workflow_set_result(
    epi_m4_xgb_model_fit,
    id = wf_id
    )
  # Select best hyperparameters by AUROC
  best_params <- select_best(wf_result, metric = "roc_auc")
  # Extract the workflow itself
  wf <- extract_workflow(epi_m4_xgb_model_fit, id = wf_id)
  # Finalize workflow with best hyperparameters
  final_wf <- finalize_workflow(wf, best_params)
  # Fit finalized workflow to derivation data
  final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = epi)
  # Collect CV metrics for the selected configuration
  cv_metrics <- collect_metrics(wf_result) |>
    filter(.config == best_params$.config)
  # Collect CV predictions for the selected configuration
  cv_predictions <- collect_predictions(wf_result) |>
    filter(.config == best_params$.config)
  # Return results
  list(
    workflow_id     = wf_id,
    best_params     = best_params,
    final_workflow  = final_wf,
    final_fit       = final_fit,
    cv_metrics      = cv_metrics,
    cv_predictions  = cv_predictions
    )
})

names(epi_m4_xgb_final_fit) <- map_chr(epi_m4_xgb_final_fit, "workflow_id")
```

Show hyperparameters resulting in the best fit.

```{r}
imap_dfr(epi_m4_xgb_final_fit, 
         ~ .x$best_params |> mutate(wflow_id = .y)
         ) |>

         ) |> 
  gt() |>

             ) |>

    align = "center",
    columns = c(trees, tree_depth, min_n, learn_rate, loss_reduction,
                sample_size, mtry
                )
    )
```

Optimal parameters are not at tuning boundaries. The algorithm preferred shallow trees with iterative small improvements (over aggressive boosting), which is consistent with the random forest findings.

### Calibration

Use the same calibration approach as in @sec-avp-cal that was used for vasopressin.

```{r}
epi_m4_xgb_preds <- epi_m4_xgb_final_fit[[1]]$cv_predictions

epi_m4_xgb_preds_cv <- epi_m4_xgb_preds |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    response = first(response),
    .pred_Response = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    response_num = if_else(response == "Response", 1, 0)
  )

set.seed(2026)
epi_xgb_cal <- pmcalibration(
  y = epi_m4_xgb_preds_cv$response_num,
  p = epi_m4_xgb_preds_cv$.pred_Response,
  ci = "boot", # n = 1000 replicates is the default
  smooth = "rcs",
  nk = 3 # 5 knots is default, 3 has less bias
  )

invisible(pdf("epi_xgboost_calibration.pdf"))
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), 
    cex.axis = 1.4, cex.lab = 1.8, cex.main = 2,
    mar = c(5.1, 5.5, 1.4, 1.6), # bottom, left, top, right
    mgp = c(3.5, 1, 0)
    )
plot(epi_xgb_cal)
invisible(dev.off())
```

The calibration of the epinephrine XGBoost model is good, with some over-prediction at higher probabilities (above ~0.4) where data are sparse.

Since the logistic regression models are generally preferred to machine learning models for this modeling goal (as noted in @sec-avp-cal) and the discrimination between models was not substantially different (AUROC for logistic regression 0.59 and for XGBoost 0.62), assess calibration for the main effects logistic regression model for comparison.

```{r}
epi_m1_lr_preds_cv <- epi_m1_lr_preds |>
  filter(wflow_id == "epi_m1_main_logistic") |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    response = first(response),
    .pred_Response = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    response_num = if_else(response == "Response", 1, 0)
  )

set.seed(2026)
epi_lr_cal <- pmcalibration(
  y = epi_m1_lr_preds_cv$response_num,
  p = epi_m1_lr_preds_cv$.pred_Response,
  ci = "boot", # n = 1000 replicates is the default
  smooth = "rcs",
  nk = 3 # 5 knots is default, 3 has less bias
  )
plot(epi_lr_cal)
title("Calibration Plot: Epinephrine Logistic Regression")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
invisible(dev.copy(pdf, "epi_logistic_calibration.pdf"))
invisible(dev.off())
```

Calibration with the main effects logistic regression model appears worse than the XGBoost model, but it is challenging to assess the upper range because of few observations.

Save the two epinephrine calibration plots as a panel figure.

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

### Decision Curve Analysis

Extract predictions from the XGBoost and logistic regression models, then combine.

```{r}
# Extract the out-of-fold predictions for each model
# Then average predictions across the 5 CV repeats using .row
# Logistic model
epi_lr_dca <- epi_m1_lr_preds |>
  filter(wflow_id == "epi_m1_main_logistic") |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    response = first(response),
    p_logistic = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# XGBoost model
epi_xgb_dca <- epi_m4_xgb_final_fit[[1]]$cv_predictions |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    p_xgb = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Combine
epi_dca_data <- epi_lr_dca |>
  left_join(epi_xgb_dca, by = ".row")
```

Then run DCA and plot.

```{r}
#| warning: false

epi_dca <- dca(
  response == "Response" ~ p_logistic + p_xgb,
  data = epi_dca_data
  )

(epi_dca_plot <- 
    ggplot(as_tibble(epi_dca) |>
             filter(net_benefit >= -0.006 &
                      net_benefit <= 0.2 &
                      threshold <=0.51
                    ) |>
             mutate(label = fct_relevel(label, "Treat None", "Treat All",
                                        "p_logistic", "p_xgb"
                                        )),
           aes(x = threshold,
               y = net_benefit,
               color = label,
               group = label)) +
    geom_smooth(method = loess, formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
      "p_logistic" = "#0072B2",
      "p_xgb" = "#7876B1FF",
      "Treat All" = "#009E73",
      "Treat None" = "#D55E00"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "p_logistic" = "Logistic regression",
        "p_xgb" = "XGBoost",
        "Treat All" = "Treat all",
        "Treat None" = "Treat none"
      )) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(-0.006, 0.2),
      expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0))
      ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0.1, 0.51),
      breaks = seq(0,0.5, by = 0.1),
      expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0.02))
      ) +
    labs(
      title = "Epinephrine Model Comparison",
      x = "Probability Threshold",
      y = "Net Benefit",
      color = NULL
      ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.33, y = 0.06, label = "Logistic model",
             color = "#0072B2", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.45, y = 0.02, label = "XGBoost model",
             color = "#7876B1FF", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.19, y = 0.07, label = "Treat all",
             color = "#009E73", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.14, y = 0.01, label = "Treat none",
             color = "#D55E00", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      axis.line.x = element_line(),
      axis.line.y = element_line(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_line(),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm")
    ))
```

Both models are better than "Treat none" and "Treat all" in the probability threshold range from about 0.2 to 0.35, the XGBoost model has higher net benefit than the logistic regression model. The XGBoost model has higher net benefit than the "Treat none" model from probability thresholds about 0.2 to about 0.45.

Obtain exact threshold values for positive net benefit with logistic regression and XGBoost models.

```{r}
as_tibble(epi_dca) |>
  select(threshold, label, net_benefit) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = label, values_from = net_benefit) |>
  filter(!is.na(p_logistic), !is.na(p_xgb), 
         !is.na(`Treat All`), !is.na(`Treat None`)
         ) |>
  summarise(
    min_prob_thresh_lr = min(threshold[p_logistic > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_logistic > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             ),
    max_prob_thresh_lr = max(threshold[p_logistic > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_logistic > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             ),
    min_prob_thresh_xgb = min(threshold[p_xgb > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_xgb > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             ),
    max_prob_thresh_xgb = max(threshold[p_xgb > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_xgb > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             )
  )
```

The epinephrine response logistic regression model had higher net benefit than the "Treat all" and "Treat none" curves at threshold probabilities from 0.16 to 0.34. The epinephrine response XGBoost model had higher net benefit than the "Treat all" and "Treat none" curves at threshold probabilities from 0.11 to 0.46 (nearly double the number of threshold probability values compared with the logistic regression model).
