### Model Selection

Among the models assessed, the boosted trees (XGBoost) machine learning model for epinephrine response demonstrated the best discrimination, overall performance, and calibration. It also had a higher net benefit in decision curve analysis than the logistic regression model. In light of these findings, the XBGoost model (`epi_m4_boost_xgboost`) was selected as the final model for epinephrine.

#### Refit to Whole Derivation Dataset

Refit the final model (`epi_m4_boost_xgboost`) in the whole epinephrine derivation dataset (`epi`).

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
epi_mod_final_wf <-
  epi_m4_xgb_final_fit[[1]]$final_workflow

epi_mod_final_fit_dev <-
  fit(epi_mod_final_wf, data = epi)
```

Estimate apparent performance on derivation data.

```{r}
# Generate predictions
epi_dev_preds <-
  predict(
    epi_mod_final_fit_dev,
    new_data = epi,
    type = "prob"
    ) |>
  bind_cols(
    epi |> select(response)
    )

epi_dev_score_data <-
  epi_dev_preds |>
  transmute(
    response_num = if_else(response == "Response", 1, 0),
    p_xgb = .pred_Response
  )

# Generate metrics 
epi_dev_score <-
  Score(
    object = list(
      "XGBoost" = epi_dev_score_data$p_xgb
    ),
    formula = response_num ~ 1,
    data = epi_dev_score_data,
    metrics = c("auc", "brier")
  )

# Extract and format results
auc_ci <-
  epi_dev_score$AUC$score |>
  as_tibble() |>
  transmute(
    auc = as.numeric(AUC),
    auc_lower = as.numeric(lower),
    auc_upper = as.numeric(upper)
  )

brier_ci <-
  epi_dev_score$Brier$score |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(model == "XGBoost") |>
  transmute(
    brier = as.numeric(Brier),
    brier_lower = as.numeric(lower),
    brier_upper = as.numeric(upper)
  )

epi_dev_mets <- cbind(auc_ci, brier_ci) |>
  mutate(
    AUROC = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", auc, auc_lower, auc_upper),
    Brier = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", brier, brier_lower, brier_upper)
  ) |>
  select(AUROC, Brier)
rm(auc_ci, brier_ci)

epi_dev_mets |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Epinephrine XGBoost Model Fit and Apparent Performance Parameters",
             subtitle = "In Derivation (Ohio) Dataset") |>
  cols_align(align = "center")
```

Notably, the apparent performance metrics for the epinephrine XGBoost model are very optimistic and substantially better than the cross-validated values (AUROC apparent 0.73 vs. CV 0.62, Brier apparent 0.18 vs. CV 0.20).

#### Compare to Simple Model

Compare the selected multivariable model (`epi_m4_boost_xgboost`) with a simple logistic regression model that only includes `neq` with a spline term.

```{r}
epi_m0_lr_rec_ns <-
  recipe(response ~ neq, data = epi) |>
  step_spline_natural(neq, deg_free = 5)

epi_m0_lr_preproc <- list(epi_m0_neq_only = epi_m0_lr_rec_ns)

epi_m0_lr_model <- 
  workflow_set(epi_m0_lr_preproc,
               list(logistic = logistic_reg(engine = "glm")), 
               cross = FALSE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(epi, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

epi_m0_lr_model_fit <- 
  epi_m0_lr_model |>
  workflow_map("fit_resamples", seed = 2026, verbose = TRUE,
               resamples = train_cv, metrics = class_metrics,
               control = keep_pred
               )
epi_m0_lr_preds <- 
  collect_predictions(epi_m0_lr_model_fit, summarize = FALSE)

epi_m0_lr_mets <- 
  collect_metrics(epi_m0_lr_model_fit) |>
  # Compute 95% Wald CIs across the 50 resamples
  mutate(
    conf.low.95 = mean - qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    conf.high.95 = mean + qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    mean_ci = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
  ) |>
  select(wflow_id, .metric, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95, mean_ci) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = c(mean_ci, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
    )

bind_rows(epi_m0_lr_mets, epi_m4_xgb_mets) |>
  select(wflow_id, mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Epinephrine Final Model Performance vs. NE Alone",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats). Presented as mean (95% CI)."
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    mean_ci_roc_auc = "AUROC",
    mean_ci_brier_class = "Brier Score",
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class)
    )
```

The multivariable model has better metrics than the simple model using `neq` alone. Using additional patient information beyond relying on norepinephrine dose alone provides meaningful improvement in the prediction of epinephrine response.

## Phenylephrine

This section will build and evaluate prediction models for response after initiation of phenylephrine as the first adjunctive vasopressor. The same approaches as for vasopressin models will be used here with less annotation. For more annotation regarding the rationale for model building and evaluation steps see @sec-avp.

### Logistic Regression

Here, use logistic regression to generate prediction models using two approaches: 1) main effects (additive) only, and 2) non-linear effects of predictors.

The two models will be built in one `workflow_set()`. First, generate a Spearman's $\rho^2$ rank correlation plot to assess for potential predictor transformation (non-linear effects).

```{r}
plot(spearman2(response ~ ., data = pe |> select(-c(age, sex, race_eth))))

invisible(pdf("pe_spearman.pdf"))
plot(spearman2(response ~ ., data = pe |> select(-c(age, sex, race_eth))),
     main = ""
     )
title(main = expression("Phenylephrine Spearman " * rho^2))
invisible(dev.off())
```

The Spearman's $\rho^2$ rank correlation plot shows that `lactate`, `map`, and `pH` have the highest potential to improve model fit with a non-linear transformation. The $\rho^2$ values for these predictors is relatively close to each other. From a biological plausibility and outcome component perspective, non-linear terms for `lactate` and `pH` are most likely to provide value. Because these two predictors are quantitative variables, introduce a natural spline with 2 knots (3 df) for `lactate` and a natural spline with 1 knot (2 df) for `pH`. This will add 3 total df to the model and spend all of the available degrees of freedom (12 df in the main effects model and 15 total available).

As noted in @sec-miss-oh, there are missing data in the same three variables as for vasopressin and epinephrine. Therefore, the same imputation approach will be used.

```{r}
# Main effects recipe
pe_m1_lr_rec_main <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = pe) |>
  # Declare age, sex, and race_eth in a bystander role 
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  # Single (linear regression) imputation for missing quantitatitve predictors
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h
                       )
                     ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map
                       )
    ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate
                       )
    )

# Non-linear effects recipe
pe_m1_lr_rec_ns <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = pe) |>
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, 
                       )
                     ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map,
                       )
    ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate,
                       )
    ) |>
  # Add natural spline with 2 knots (3 df) for lactate
  step_spline_natural(lactate, deg_free = 3) |>
  # Add natural spline with 1 knot (2 df) for pH
  step_spline_natural(pH, deg_free = 2) 

# Set up pre-processing and model workflow_set()
pe_m1_lr_preproc <- list(
  pe_m1_main = pe_m1_lr_rec_main, 
  pe_m1_ns = pe_m1_lr_rec_ns
  )

pe_m1_lr_models <- 
  workflow_set(pe_m1_lr_preproc,
               list(logistic = logistic_reg(engine = "glm")), 
               cross = FALSE)

# Resample each model in the set with 10-fold CV (5 repeats)
set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(pe, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

pe_m1_lr_models_fit <- 
  pe_m1_lr_models |>
  workflow_map("fit_resamples", seed = 2026, verbose = TRUE,
               resamples = train_cv, metrics = class_metrics,
               control = keep_pred
               )

# Collect predictions
pe_m1_lr_preds <- 
  collect_predictions(pe_m1_lr_models_fit, summarize = FALSE)

# Collect then show the metrics
pe_m1_lr_mets <- 
  collect_metrics(pe_m1_lr_models_fit) |>
  mutate(
    conf.low.95 = mean - qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    conf.high.95 = mean + qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    mean_ci = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
  ) |>
  select(wflow_id, .metric, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95, mean_ci) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = c(mean_ci, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
    )

pe_m1_lr_mets |>
  select(wflow_id, mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Phenylephrine m1 (Logistic Regression) Metric Comparison",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats). Presented as mean (95% CI)."
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    mean_ci_roc_auc = "AUROC",
    mean_ci_brier_class = "Brier Score",
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class)
    )
```

The two logistic regression modeling approaches had essentially the same discrimination (AUROC) and overall performance (Brier score).

```{r}
pe_m1_lr_preds |>
  group_by(wflow_id) |>
  roc_curve(response, .pred_Response) |>
  autoplot()
```

The two curves are essentially overlapping.

### Machine Learning

#### Regularized (Elastic Net)

Fit regularized (elastic net) models.

```{r}
pe_m2_rec_main <- pe_m1_lr_rec_main |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

pe_m2_rec_ns <- pe_m1_lr_rec_ns |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

pe_m2_glmnet_preproc <- list(
  pe_m2_main = pe_m2_rec_main, 
  pe_m2_ns = pe_m2_rec_ns
  )

pe_m2_glmnet_models <- 
  workflow_set(pe_m2_glmnet_preproc,
               list(glmnet = logistic_reg(
                 engine = "glmnet",
                 mode = "classification",
                 penalty = tune(),     # lambda
                 mixture = tune()      # alpha
                 )),
               cross = TRUE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(pe, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

pen_grid <- grid_space_filling(
  penalty(range = c(-5, 0)), # log10 scale, reasonable range for elastic net
  mixture(range = c(0, 1)),  # default
  size = 30
  )

pe_m2_glmnet_models_fit <- 
  pe_m2_glmnet_models |> 
  workflow_map("tune_grid", seed = 2026, verbose = TRUE,
               resamples = train_cv, grid = pen_grid,
               metrics = class_metrics, control = keep_pred
               )

workflow_ids <- pe_m2_glmnet_models_fit$wflow_id

# Loop over workflows to finalize, fit, and collect results
pe_m2_glmnet_final_fit <- map(workflow_ids, function(wf_id) {
  
  # Extract tuning results for this workflow
  wf_result <- extract_workflow_set_result(pe_m2_glmnet_models_fit, id = wf_id)
  
  # Get best parameters by AUROC
  best_params <- select_best(wf_result, metric = "roc_auc")
  
  # Extract the workflow object itself
  wf <- extract_workflow(pe_m2_glmnet_models_fit, id = wf_id)
  
  # Finalize the workflow with best hyperparameters
  final_wf <- finalize_workflow(
    wf,
    best_params
  )
  
  # Fit the final workflow to the training set
  final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = pe)
  
  # Collect resampling metrics for this workflow from tuning
  cv_metrics <- collect_metrics(wf_result) |>
    filter(penalty == best_params$penalty,
           mixture == best_params$mixture)
  
  # Collect predictions for the best parameters
  cv_preds <- collect_predictions(wf_result, summarize = TRUE) |>
    filter(penalty == best_params$penalty,
           mixture == best_params$mixture)
  
  # Return as a list
  list(
    workflow_id = wf_id,
    best_params = best_params,
    final_workflow = final_wf,
    final_fit = final_fit,
    cv_metrics = cv_metrics,
    cv_predictions = cv_preds
  )
})

# Name the list elements by workflow
names(pe_m2_glmnet_final_fit) <- workflow_ids
rm(workflow_ids)
```

Show elastic net hyperparameters resulting in the best fit.

```{r}
imap_dfr(pe_m2_glmnet_final_fit, 
         ~ .x$best_params |> mutate(wflow_id = .y)
         ) |>
  select(wflow_id, penalty, mixture) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Phenylephrine m2 Elastic Net Best Hyperparameters",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats)"
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    penalty = "Penalty (lambda [λ])",
    mixture = "Mixture (alpha [α])"
    ) |>
  fmt_number(decimals = 4) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(penalty, mixture)
    )
```

Collect metrics and display table (comparing to the logistic regression model fits).

The regularized (elastic net) models performed slightly better than the logistic regression models.

#### Random Forest

Fit a random forest model.

```{r}
pe_m3_rf_rec <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = pe) |>
  # Declare age, sex, race_eth in a bystander role to keep it in the 
  # resampling dataset for future use in fairness checks
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  # Single (linear regression) imputation for missing quantitative predictors
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h
                       )
                     ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map
                       )
    ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era, criteria_met, 
                       sofa2_no_cv, neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate
                       )
    )

pe_m3_rf_preproc <- list(pe_m3_rf = pe_m3_rf_rec)

pe_m3_rf_models <- 
  workflow_set(pe_m3_rf_preproc,
               list(ranger = rand_forest(
                 engine = "ranger",
                 mode = "classification",
                 trees = 1000,      # Default is 500, 1000 is better      
                 mtry = tune(),     # Number of randomly selected predictors     
                 min_n = tune()     # Minimum node size   
                 )),
               cross = TRUE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(pe, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

# Prep recipe and determine predictor count
pe_m3_rf_rec_prep <- prep(pe_m3_rf_rec)

x_train <- bake(pe_m3_rf_rec_prep, new_data = NULL) |>
  select(-c(response, age, sex, race_eth))

p <- ncol(x_train) # p == 10

rf_param_set <- parameters(
  mtry(range = c(1L, 10L)), #sqrt(p) ~= 3, (p / 2) == 5, which is too narrow
  min_n(range = c(2L, 100L)) # Expanded range (50L used for other medications) 
                             # because optimal parameters were at boundary
                             # and performance was improving.
)

initial_candidates <- grid_space_filling(
  rf_param_set,
  size = 30
)

race_ctrl <- control_race(
  save_pred = TRUE,
  save_workflow = TRUE,
  parallel_over = "resamples",
  verbose = FALSE
)

pe_m3_rf_model_fit <-
  pe_m3_rf_models |>
  workflow_map(
    "tune_race_anova", seed = 2026, resamples = train_cv,
    grid = initial_candidates, metrics = class_metrics, control = race_ctrl
  )

# Get workflow IDs
workflow_ids <- pe_m3_rf_model_fit$wflow_id

# Finalize, fit, and collect results for the workflow
pe_m3_rf_final_fit <- map(workflow_ids, function(wf_id) {
  # Extract tuning (race) results for this workflow
  wf_result <- extract_workflow_set_result(
    pe_m3_rf_model_fit,
    id = wf_id
    )
  # Select best hyperparameters by AUROC
  best_params <- select_best(wf_result, metric = "roc_auc")
  # Extract the workflow itself
  wf <- extract_workflow(pe_m3_rf_model_fit, id = wf_id)
  # Finalize workflow with best hyperparameters
  final_wf <- finalize_workflow(wf, best_params)
  # Fit finalized workflow to derivation data
  final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = pe)
  # Collect CV metrics for the selected configuration
  cv_metrics <- collect_metrics(wf_result) |>
    filter(.config == best_params$.config)
  # Collect CV predictions for the selected configuration
  cv_predictions <- collect_predictions(wf_result) |>
    filter(.config == best_params$.config)
  # Return results
  list(
    workflow_id     = wf_id,
    best_params     = best_params,
    final_workflow  = final_wf,
    final_fit       = final_fit,
    cv_metrics      = cv_metrics,
    cv_predictions  = cv_predictions
    )
})

names(pe_m3_rf_final_fit) <- map_chr(pe_m3_rf_final_fit, "workflow_id")
```

Show hyperparameters resulting in the best fit.

```{r}
imap_dfr(pe_m3_rf_final_fit, 
         ~ .x$best_params |> mutate(workflow_id = .y)
         ) |>
  select(workflow_id, mtry, min_n) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Random Forest Best Hyperparameters",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats)"
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    workflow_id = "Model",
    mtry = "Random Variables at Split (mtry)",
    min_n = "Min Terminal Node Size (min_n)"
    ) |>
  fmt_number(decimals = 0) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(workflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(mtry, min_n)
    )
```

Although min_n is at the top of the range, performance did not continue to improve as min_n approached the top of the range (not shown). Therefore these were accepted as the final parameters.

#### Boosted Trees

Generate a boosted tree model.

```{r}
pe_m4_xgb_rec <-
  recipe(response ~ ., data = pe) |>
  update_role(age, sex, race_eth, new_role = "bystander") |>
  step_impute_linear(
    map,
    impute_with = vars(
      heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era,
      criteria_met, sofa2_no_cv,
      neq, shock_dur_h
    )
  ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    lactate,
    impute_with = vars(
      heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era,
      criteria_met, sofa2_no_cv,
      neq, shock_dur_h, map
    )
  ) |>
  step_impute_linear(
    pH,
    impute_with = vars(
      heart_failure, tx_unit, ssc_era,
      criteria_met, sofa2_no_cv,
      neq, shock_dur_h, map, lactate
    )
  ) |>
  # Dummy code nominal predictors
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

pe_m4_xgb_preproc <- list(pe_m4_boost = pe_m4_xgb_rec)

pe_m4_xgb_model <- 
  workflow_set(pe_m4_xgb_preproc,
               list(xgboost = boost_tree(
                 trees = 1000,              # Number of trees       
                 tree_depth = tune(),       # Tree depth: # of "interactions" 
                 min_n = tune(),            # Minimum node size
                 loss_reduction = tune(),   # Reduction in the loss function required to split further
                 sample_size = tune(),      # Proportion of data exposed to fitting routine
                 mtry = tune(),             # Random predictors at each split
                 learn_rate = tune()        # Rate at which the boosting algorithm adapts
                 ) |>
                   set_engine("xgboost") |>  
                   set_mode("classification")
                 ),
               cross = FALSE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(pe, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

# Prep recipe and determine post-dummy predictor count
pe_m4_xgb_rec_prep <- prep(pe_m4_xgb_rec)

x_train <- bake(pe_m4_xgb_rec_prep, new_data = NULL) |>
  select(-c(response, age, sex, race_eth))

p <- ncol(x_train) # p == 10

# Select parameters (particularly depth) based p==10 and RF optimal parameters
xgb_params <- parameters(
  tree_depth(range = c(1L, 6L)),
  min_n(range = c(2L, 50L)),
  learn_rate(range = c(-3, -0.5)),
  loss_reduction(),
  sample_prop(range = c(0.5, 1.0)),
  finalize(mtry(), x_train)
  )

initial_candidates <- grid_space_filling(
  xgb_params,
  size = 30
  )

race_ctrl <- control_race(
  save_pred = TRUE,
  save_workflow = TRUE,
  parallel_over = "resamples",
  verbose = FALSE
  )

pe_m4_xgb_model_fit <-
  pe_m4_xgb_model |>
  workflow_map(
    "tune_race_anova",
    seed = 2026,
    resamples = train_cv,
    grid = initial_candidates,
    metrics = class_metrics,
    control = race_ctrl
    )

workflow_ids <- pe_m4_xgb_model_fit$wflow_id

# Finalize, fit, and collect results the workflow
pe_m4_xgb_final_fit <- map(workflow_ids, function(wf_id) {
  # Extract tuning (race) results for this workflow
  wf_result <- extract_workflow_set_result(
    pe_m4_xgb_model_fit,
    id = wf_id
    )
  # Select best hyperparameters by AUROC
  best_params <- select_best(wf_result, metric = "roc_auc")
  # Extract the workflow itself
  wf <- extract_workflow(pe_m4_xgb_model_fit, id = wf_id)
  # Finalize workflow with best hyperparameters
  final_wf <- finalize_workflow(wf, best_params)
  # Fit finalized workflow to derivation data
  final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = pe)
  # Collect CV metrics for the selected configuration
  cv_metrics <- collect_metrics(wf_result) |>
    filter(.config == best_params$.config)
  # Collect CV predictions for the selected configuration
  cv_predictions <- collect_predictions(wf_result) |>
    filter(.config == best_params$.config)
  # Return results
  list(
    workflow_id     = wf_id,
    best_params     = best_params,
    final_workflow  = final_wf,
    final_fit       = final_fit,
    cv_metrics      = cv_metrics,
    cv_predictions  = cv_predictions
    )
})

names(pe_m4_xgb_final_fit) <- map_chr(pe_m4_xgb_final_fit, "workflow_id")
```

### Calibration

Use the same calibration approach as in @sec-avp-cal that was used for vasopressin (and for epinephrine).

Start with calibration for the logistic regression (main effects) model.

```{r}
pe_m1_lr_preds_cv <- pe_m1_lr_preds |>
  filter(wflow_id == "pe_m1_main_logistic") |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    response = first(response),
    .pred_Response = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    response_num = if_else(response == "Response", 1, 0)
  )

set.seed(2026)
pe_lr_cal <- pmcalibration(
  y = pe_m1_lr_preds_cv$response_num,
  p = pe_m1_lr_preds_cv$.pred_Response,
  ci = "boot", # n = 1000 replicates is the default
  smooth = "rcs",
  nk = 3 # 5 knots is default, 3 has less bias
  )
plot(pe_lr_cal)
title("Calibration Plot: Phenylephrine Logistic Regression")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
invisible(dev.copy(pdf, "pe_logistic_calibration.pdf"))
invisible(dev.off())
```

Calibration with the logistic regression model is pretty good.

Next, assess calibration with the random forest model.

```{r}
pe_m3_rf_preds <- pe_m3_rf_final_fit[[1]]$cv_predictions

pe_m3_rf_preds_cv <- pe_m3_rf_preds |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    response = first(response),
    .pred_Response = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    response_num = if_else(response == "Response", 1, 0)
  )

set.seed(2026)
pe_rf_cal <- pmcalibration(
  y = pe_m3_rf_preds_cv$response_num,
  p = pe_m3_rf_preds_cv$.pred_Response,
  ci = "boot", # n = 1000 replicates is the default
  smooth = "rcs",
  nk = 3 # 5 knots is default, 3 has less bias
  )
invisible(pdf("pe_rf_calibration.pdf"))
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), 
    cex.axis = 1.4, cex.lab = 1.8, cex.main = 2,
    mar = c(5.1, 5.5, 1.4, 1.6), # bottom, left, top, right
    mgp = c(3.5, 1, 0)
    )
plot(pe_rf_cal)
invisible(dev.off())
```

Calibration of the phenylephrine random forest model is very good to excellent.

### Decision Curve Analysis

Extract predictions from the logistic regression and random forest models, then combine.

```{r}
# Extract the out-of-fold predictions for each model
# Then average predictions across the 5 CV repeats using .row
# Logistic model
pe_lr_dca <- pe_m1_lr_preds |>
  filter(wflow_id == "pe_m1_main_logistic") |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    response = first(response),
    p_logistic = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Random forest model
pe_rf_dca <- pe_m3_rf_final_fit[[1]]$cv_predictions |>
  group_by(.row) |>
  summarise(
    p_rf = mean(.pred_Response),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Combine
pe_dca_data <- pe_lr_dca |>
  left_join(pe_rf_dca, by = ".row")
```

Then run DCA and plot.

```{r}
#| warning: false

pe_dca <- dca(
  response == "Response" ~ p_logistic + p_rf,
  data = pe_dca_data
  )

(pe_dca_plot <- 
    ggplot(as_tibble(pe_dca) |>
             filter(net_benefit >= -0.006 &
                      net_benefit <= 0.31 &
                      threshold <=0.55
                    ) |>
             mutate(label = fct_relevel(label, "Treat None", "Treat All",
                                        "p_logistic", "p_rf"
                                        )),
           aes(x = threshold,
               y = net_benefit,
               color = label,
               group = label)) +
    geom_smooth(method = loess, formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
      "p_logistic" = "#0072B2",
      "p_rf" = "#7876B1FF",
      "Treat All" = "#009E73",
      "Treat None" = "#D55E00"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "p_logistic" = "Logistic regression",
        "p_rf" = "Random forest",
        "Treat All" = "Treat all",
        "Treat None" = "Treat none"
      )) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(-0.006, 0.31),
      expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0))
      ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0.1, 0.55),
      breaks = seq(0,0.55, by = 0.1),
      expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0.02))
      ) +
    labs(
      title = "Phenylephrine Model Comparison",
      x = "Probability Threshold",
      y = "Net Benefit",
      color = NULL
      ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.44, y = 0.09, label = "Logistic model",
             color = "#0072B2", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.38, y = 0.15, label = "Random forest model",
             color = "#7876B1FF", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.27, y = 0.07, label = "Treat all",
             color = "#009E73", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.14, y = 0.01, label = "Treat none",
             color = "#D55E00", family = "sans", fontface = "bold", 
             size = 4
             ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      axis.line.x = element_line(),
      axis.line.y = element_line(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_line(),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm")
    ))
```

Both models are better than "Treat none" and "Treat all" in the probability threshold range from about 0.2 to 0.5, the random forest model has slightly higher net benefit than the logistic regression model.

Obtain exact threshold values for positive net benefit with logistic regression and random forest models. Filter threshold values to those corresponding to the first instance the curve crosses zero net benefit.

```{r}
as_tibble(pe_dca) |>
  select(threshold, label, net_benefit) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = label, values_from = net_benefit) |>
  filter(!is.na(p_logistic), !is.na(p_rf), 
         !is.na(`Treat All`), !is.na(`Treat None`), 
         threshold <0.6
         ) |>
  summarise(
    min_prob_thresh_lr = min(threshold[p_logistic > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_logistic > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             ),
    max_prob_thresh_lr = max(threshold[p_logistic > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_logistic > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             ),
    min_prob_thresh_rf = min(threshold[p_rf > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_rf > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             ),
    max_prob_thresh_rf = max(threshold[p_rf > `Treat All` + 0.001 & 
                                         p_rf > `Treat None` + 0.001]
                             )
  )
```

The phenylephrine response logistic regression model had higher net benefit than the "Treat all" and "Treat none" curves at threshold probabilities from 0.16 to 0.5. The phenylephrine response random forest model had higher net benefit than the "Treat all" and "Treat none" curves at threshold probabilities from 0.2 to 0.55. The range of these values are similar (0.34 and 0.35, respectively).

### Model Selection

Among the models assessed, the random forest machine learning model for phenylephrine response demonstrated the best discrimination (similar to XGBoost), overall performance, and calibration. It also had a slightly higher net benefit in decision curve analysis than the logistic regression model. In light of these findings, the random forest model (`pe_m3_rf_ranger`) was selected as the final model for phenylephrine.

#### Refit to Whole Derivation Dataset

Refit the final model (`pe_m3_rf_ranger`) in the whole epinephrine derivation dataset (`pe`).

```{r}
set.seed(2026)
pe_mod_final_wf <-
  pe_m3_rf_final_fit[[1]]$final_workflow

pe_mod_final_fit_dev <-
  fit(pe_mod_final_wf, data = pe)
```

Estimate apparent performance on derivation data.

```{r}
# Generate predictions
pe_dev_preds <-
  predict(
    pe_mod_final_fit_dev,
    new_data = pe,
    type = "prob"
    ) |>
  bind_cols(
    pe |> select(response)
    )

pe_dev_score_data <-
  pe_dev_preds |>
  transmute(
    response_num = if_else(response == "Response", 1, 0),
    p_rf = .pred_Response
  )

# Generate metrics 
pe_dev_score <-
  Score(
    object = list(
      "Random Forest" = pe_dev_score_data$p_rf
    ),
    formula = response_num ~ 1,
    data = pe_dev_score_data,
    metrics = c("auc", "brier")
  )

# Extract and format results
auc_ci <-
  pe_dev_score$AUC$score |>
  as_tibble() |>
  transmute(
    auc = as.numeric(AUC),
    auc_lower = as.numeric(lower),
    auc_upper = as.numeric(upper)
  )

brier_ci <-
  pe_dev_score$Brier$score |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(model == "Random Forest") |>
  transmute(
    brier = as.numeric(Brier),
    brier_lower = as.numeric(lower),
    brier_upper = as.numeric(upper)
  )

pe_dev_mets <- cbind(auc_ci, brier_ci) |>
  mutate(
    AUROC = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", auc, auc_lower, auc_upper),
    Brier = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", brier, brier_lower, brier_upper)
  ) |>
  select(AUROC, Brier)
rm(auc_ci, brier_ci)

pe_dev_mets |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Phenylephrine Random Forest Model Fit and Apparent Performance Parameters",
             subtitle = "In Derivation (Ohio) Dataset") |>
  cols_align(align = "center")
```

Similar to epinephrine, the apparent performance metrics for the phenylephrine random forest model are very optimistic and substantially better than the cross-validated values (AUROC apparent 0.84 vs. CV 0.66, Brier apparent 0.17 vs. CV 0.22).

#### Compare to Simple Model

Compare the selected multivariable model (`pe_m3_rf_ranger`) with a simple logistic regression model that only includes `neq` with a spline term.

```{r}
pe_m0_lr_rec_ns <-
  recipe(response ~ neq, data = pe) |>
  step_spline_natural(neq, deg_free = 5)

pe_m0_lr_preproc <- list(pe_m0_neq_only = pe_m0_lr_rec_ns)

pe_m0_lr_model <- 
  workflow_set(pe_m0_lr_preproc,
               list(logistic = logistic_reg(engine = "glm")), 
               cross = FALSE
               )

set.seed(2026)
train_cv <- vfold_cv(pe, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = response)
class_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, brier_class)
keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = FALSE)

pe_m0_lr_model_fit <- 
  pe_m0_lr_model |>
  workflow_map("fit_resamples", seed = 2026, verbose = TRUE,
               resamples = train_cv, metrics = class_metrics,
               control = keep_pred
               )
pe_m0_lr_preds <- 
  collect_predictions(pe_m0_lr_model_fit, summarize = FALSE)

pe_m0_lr_mets <- 
  collect_metrics(pe_m0_lr_model_fit) |>
  # Compute 95% Wald CIs across the 50 resamples
  mutate(
    conf.low.95 = mean - qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    conf.high.95 = mean + qt(0.975, df = 10*5-1) * std_err,
    mean_ci = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
  ) |>
  select(wflow_id, .metric, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95, mean_ci) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = c(mean_ci, mean, conf.low.95, conf.high.95)
    )

bind_rows(pe_m0_lr_mets, pe_m3_rf_mets) |>
  select(wflow_id, mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Phenylephrine Final Model Performance vs. NE Alone",
    subtitle = "Using 10-fold Cross-Validation (5 repeats). Presented as mean (95% CI)."
    ) |>
  cols_label(
    wflow_id = "Model",
    mean_ci_roc_auc = "AUROC",
    mean_ci_brier_class = "Brier Score",
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = c(wflow_id)
    ) |>
  cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = c(mean_ci_roc_auc, mean_ci_brier_class)
    )
```

The multivariable model has better metrics than the simple model using `neq` alone. Using additional patient information beyond relying on norepinephrine dose alone provides meaningful improvement in the prediction of phenylephrine response.

# Final Model Descriptors

## Permutation Importance

Here, address the question "Which variables matter for the prediction models?". Approach this question with permutation importance.

First, define a prediction wrapper. Then, use the `vi()` function from the `{vip}` package to determine variable importance based on AUROC through 100 simulations. The output of the function can roughly be interpreted as the average decrease in AUROC when that variable is randomly permuted

```{r}
pred_fun <- function(object, newdata) {
  predict(
    object,
    new_data = newdata,
    type = "prob"
    )$.pred_Response
  }

avp_vi <- vi(
  avp_mod_final_fit_dev,
  method = "permute",
  target = "response",
  metric = roc_auc_vec,
  pred_wrapper = pred_fun,
  train = avp,
  nsim = 100,
  smaller_is_better = FALSE
  ) |>
  mutate(model = factor("Vasopressin Logistic Regression"))

epi_vi <- vi(
  epi_mod_final_fit_dev,
  method = "permute",
  target = "response",
  metric = roc_auc_vec,
  pred_wrapper = pred_fun,
  train = epi,
  nsim = 100,
  smaller_is_better = FALSE
  ) |>
  mutate(model = factor("Epinephrine XGBoost"))

pe_vi <- vi(
  pe_mod_final_fit_dev,
  method = "permute",
  target = "response",
  metric = roc_auc_vec,
  pred_wrapper = pred_fun,
  train = pe,
  nsim = 100,
  smaller_is_better = FALSE
  ) |>
  mutate(model = factor("Phenylephrine Random Forest"))

all_vi <- bind_rows(avp_vi, epi_vi, pe_vi) |>
  filter(Variable != "age" & Variable != "sex" & Variable != "race_eth") |>
  group_by(model) |>
  arrange(desc(Importance), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  ungroup()
```

Then plot variable importance for each model.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 7

(vip_plot <- ggplot(all_vi,
                   aes(x = Importance, 
                       y = reorder_within(Variable, Importance, model)
                       )
                   ) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  labs(y = NULL))
```

This plot shows that `neq` dominates the vasopressin model and has the highest importance in the epinephrine model, whereas `map` and `lactate` become relatively more important in the phenylephrine model.

Save plot.

```{r}
ggsave(
  "variable_importance_plot.tiff",
  plot = vip_plot,
  device = ragg::agg_tiff,
  width = 5,
  height = 6,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
  )
```


## Feature Importance

Here, address the question "How do the variables (features) influence individual predictions?". Approach this question with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values.

First, isolate predictor data used by each fitted model.

```{r}
avp_x <- avp |> select(-response)
epi_x <- epi |> select(-response)
pe_x <- pe |> select(-response)
```

Then, build SHAP values and plot with a beeswarm plot.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 7

pred_fun <- function(object, newdata) {
  predict(
    object,
    new_data = newdata,
    type = "prob"
  )$.pred_Response
  }

shap_epi <- fastshap::explain(
  epi_mod_final_fit_dev,
  X = epi_x,
  pred_wrapper = pred_fun,
  nsim = 200)
shap_epi <- shap_epi[, colnames(shap_epi) != "age"]
shap_epi <- shap_epi[, colnames(shap_epi) != "sex"]
shap_epi <- shap_epi[, colnames(shap_epi) != "race_eth"]

sv_epi <- shapviz(
  shap_epi,
  X = epi_x |> select(-c(age, sex, race_eth))
  )

epi_shap <- sv_importance(sv_epi, kind = "beeswarm") +
  labs(title =  "Epinephrine XGBoost")

shap_pe <- fastshap::explain(
  pe_mod_final_fit_dev,
  X = pe_x,
  pred_wrapper = pred_fun,
  nsim = 200)
shap_pe <- shap_pe[, colnames(shap_pe) != "age"]
shap_pe <- shap_pe[, colnames(shap_pe) != "sex"]
shap_pe <- shap_pe[, colnames(shap_pe) != "race_eth"]

sv_pe <- shapviz(
  shap_pe,
  X = pe_x |> select(-c(age, sex, race_eth))
  )

pe_shap <- sv_importance(sv_pe, kind = "beeswarm") +
  labs(title =  "Phenylephrine Random Forest")

(shap_panel <- epi_shap / pe_shap)
rm(avp_x, epi_x, pe_x, shap_epi, sv_epi, epi_shap, shap_pe, sv_pe, pe_shap)
```

Save plot.

```{r}
ggsave(
  "shap_beeswarm_panel.tiff",
  plot = shap_panel,
  device = ragg::agg_tiff,
  width = 5,
  height = 6,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
  )
```

## Model Performance by Subgroup

Here, assess model apparent performance (AUROC and Brier score) across clinically important subgroups. Utilize the out-of-fold predictions from each model, which corrects for optimism. Specifically, evaluate subgroup performance using out-of-fold predictions 10-fold cross-validation averaged over the 5 repeats. Then, obtain confidence intervals using 500 bootstrap resamples within each subgroup.

First, define a function to evaluate the models through bootstrap resampling (500 resamples). Then, define a function to create a reusable prediction helper.

```{r}
boot_classification_by_group <- function(
    preds,
    outcome,
    prob_col,
    group_var,
    positive_level = "Response",
    B = 500,
    seed = 2026
    ) {

  set.seed(seed)

  split_data <- split(preds, preds[[group_var]])

  results <- map(
    split_data,
    function(dat) {
      n <- nrow(dat)
      group_level <- dat[[group_var]][1]
      boot_res <- replicate(
        B,
        {idx <- sample.int(n, replace = TRUE)
          boot_dat <- dat[idx, ]
          auc_val <-
            if (length(unique(boot_dat[[outcome]])) < 2) {
              NA_real_
              } else {
                roc_auc_vec(
                  truth = boot_dat[[outcome]],
                  estimate = boot_dat[[prob_col]],
                  event_level = "first"
                  )
                }
          brier_val <-
            mean(
              (as.integer(boot_dat[[outcome]] == positive_level) -
                 boot_dat[[prob_col]]
               )^2
              )
          c(auc = auc_val, brier = brier_val)
          }
        )

      boot_res <- t(boot_res) |> as_tibble()
      
      auc_na_prop <-
        if (length(boot_res$auc) > 0) {
          mean(is.na(boot_res$auc))
          } else {
            NA_real_
            }
      auc_hat <-
        roc_auc_vec(truth = dat[[outcome]], estimate = dat[[prob_col]],
                    event_level = "first"
                    )
      brier_hat <-
        mean(
          (as.integer(dat[[outcome]] == positive_level) - dat[[prob_col]])^2
          )
      auc_ci <-
        quantile(boot_res$auc, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
      brier_ci <-
        quantile(boot_res$brier, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
      list(
        summary =
          tibble(
            !!group_var := group_level,
            n = n,
            events = sum(dat[[outcome]] == positive_level),
            event_rate = events / n,
            auc_est = auc_hat,
            auc_low = auc_ci[1],
            auc_high = auc_ci[2],
            brier_est = brier_hat,
            brier_low = brier_ci[1],
            brier_high = brier_ci[2],
                        auc_na_prop = auc_na_prop
            ),
        boot =
          boot_res |>
          mutate(!!group_var := group_level)
        )
      }
    )

  list(
    summary = bind_rows(map(results, "summary")),
    boot = bind_rows(map(results, "boot"))
    )
  }

get_group_predictions <- function(
    fit_obj, data, outcome_var, group_var
    ) {
  
  probs <-
    predict(
      fit_obj,
      new_data = data,
      type = "prob"
      )
  bind_cols(
    data |> select(all_of(outcome_var), all_of(group_var)),
    probs
    )
  }
```

    group_order = factor(
      group_label,

                 "Sex: Male", "Race/Ethnicity: Black, non-Hispanic", 
                 "Race/Ethnicity: Hispanic or Other race",

  select(medication, variable, group_label, auc_est, auc_low, auc_high,
         brier_est, brier_low, brier_high, group_order
         ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^(auc|brier)_"),
    names_to = c("metric", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(auc|brier)_(est|low|high)"
    ) |>
  mutate(
    metric = recode(metric, auc = "AUROC", brier = "Brier Score"),
    medication = factor(
      medication,
      levels = c("Vasopressin", "Epinephrine", "Phenylephrine")
      ),
    variable = factor(variable, levels = c("Age", "Sex", "Race/Ethnicity"))
    )

# Decision Model Validation

The decision model will be validated in the validation (`fl`) dataset using a discordance analysis framework as described in [Dalton 2016](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0272989X15578835). First, the dataset will be described. Next, the final models for each vasopressor (vasopressin == logistic regression with spline term (`avp_m1_ns_logistic`), epinephrine == gradient boosted trees with XGBoost (`epi_m4_boost_xgboost`), phenylephrine == random forest (`pe_m3_rf_ranger`)) will be applied to each observation in the validation dataset. The vasopressor with the highest predicted probability of response will be considered the decision model-recommended vasopressor. Then, this recommended therapy will be compared to the observed treatment the patient received during usual care. Concordance will be defined as receipt of the adjunctive vasopressor recommended by the decision model, whereas discordance will be defined as receipt of a different adjunctive vasopressor. Observed outcomes will be compared between concordant and discordant treatment decisions. The discordance analysis will estimate the global effectiveness of the decision model, defined as the odds ratio for hemodynamic response at 6 hours comparing concordant and discordant therapy using logistic regression.

Subgroup and sensitivity analyses for the decision model effectiveness will be performed. In the first subgroup analysis, concordance effectiveness will be evaluated according to the specific adjunctive vasopressor recommended by the decision model. In the second and third subgroup analyses, concordance effectiveness will be assessed in relation to decision model recommendation strength, defined by the difference in predicted response probabilities between the highest- and second-highest-ranked therapies and by quartiles of the corresponding decision model odds ratio, respectively. In the first sensitivity analysis, practical equivalence of probabilities will be considered for the medications with difference in predicted response probability zones of ≤0.05 or ≤0.10 compared with the highest-ranked therapy. Receipt of any therapy with a probability in the zone will be considered concordant. In the second sensitivity analysis, only vasopressin and epinephrine will be considered eligible adjunctive vasopressors in the decision model, consistent with current guideline recommendations.

## Create and Assess Decision Model {#sec-create-dm}

Generate predicted response probability in the validation dataset (`fl`) using the final clinical prediction models for response to vasopressin (logistic regression with a spline term for NEQ; `avp_m1_ns_logistic`), epinephrine (boosted trees with XGBoost; `epi_m4_boost_xgboost`), and phenylephrine (random forest; `pe_m3_rf_ranger`).

```{r}
avp_val_preds <-
  predict(
    avp_mod_final_fit_dev,
    new_data = fl,
    type = "prob"
    ) |>
  select(avp_pred_response_prob = .pred_Response)

epi_val_preds <-
  predict(
    epi_mod_final_fit_dev,
    new_data = fl,
    type = "prob"
    ) |>
  select(epi_pred_response_prob = .pred_Response)

pe_val_preds <-
  predict(
    pe_mod_final_fit_dev,
    new_data = fl,
    type = "prob"
    ) |>
  select(pe_pred_response_prob = .pred_Response)

fl_aug <-
  cbind(fl, avp_val_preds, epi_val_preds, pe_val_preds)
# Remove objects that won't be used moving forward
rm(avp_val_preds, epi_val_preds, pe_val_preds)
```

## Decision Model Recommendation

Determine decision model-recommended adjunctive vasopressor medication (`rec_first_adj`), defined as the first adjunctive vasopressor with the highest (maximum) predicted probability of response.

```{r}
fl_aug <- fl_aug |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    best_prob = max(avp_pred_response_prob, epi_pred_response_prob, 
        pe_pred_response_prob
        ),
    rec_first_adj = factor(case_when(
      best_prob == avp_pred_response_prob ~ "vasopressin",
      best_prob == epi_pred_response_prob ~ "epinephrine",
      best_prob == pe_pred_response_prob ~ "phenylephrine",
      .default = "Error"
      ),
      levels = c("vasopressin", "epinephrine", "phenylephrine")
      )
    ) |>
  ungroup()
```

Show a table of the decision model-recommended adjunctive vasopressor medication (`rec_first_adj`).

```{r}
fl_aug |> tabyl(rec_first_adj) |>
  adorn_totals() |>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |>
  rename(Recommended = rec_first_adj) |>
  kable(align = c('lcc'),
        caption = "Decision Model-Recommended Adjunctive Vasopressor (Validation Cohort)"
        ) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

The most commonly recommended first adjunctive vasopressor medication in the validation (Florida) dataset was phenylephrine.

Show a table of recommended first adjunctive vasopressor medication vs. the first adjunctive vasopressor medication received during the patient's observed course of care.

```{r}
fl_aug |> tabyl(first_adj, rec_first_adj) |>
  adorn_totals(where = c("row", "col")) |> 
  adorn_percentages(denominator = "col")|>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |>
  adorn_ns(position = "front") |>
  adorn_title(placement = "combined") |>
  rename("Received (row)/Recommended (col)" = `first_adj/rec_first_adj`) |>
  kable(align = c('lcc'),
        caption = "Decision Model-Recommended Adjunctive Vasopressor vs. Received Adjunct"
        ) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

An adjunctive vasopressor other than the model-recommended vasopressor (discordance) was observed for 24 of 323 (7.4%) patients recommended to receive vasopressin, 297 of 323 (92%) patients recommended to receive epinephrine, and 448 of 482 (92.9%) patients recommended to receive phenylephrine.

Inversely, of the 976 patients who received vasopressin, 299 (30.6%) patients received the model recommendation-concordant adjunctive vasopressor (vasopressin) and 69.4% received a discordant adjunctive vasopressor. Of the 95 patients who received epinephrine, 26 (27.4%) patients received the model recommendation-concordant adjunctive vasopressor (epinephrine) and 69 patients (72.6%) received a discordant adjunctive vasopressor. Of the 57 patients who received phenylephrine, 34 (59.6%) patients received the model recommendation-concordant adjunctive vasopressor (phenylephrine) and 23 (40.4%) patients received a discordant adjunctive vasopressor. 

Plot the concordance between model-recommended first adjunctive vasopressor and the treatment (adjunctive vasopressor) received using an alluvial plot.

## Discordance analysis

### Primary analysis

Perform a discordance analysis and sensitivity analyses as described in [Dalton 2016](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0272989X15578835).

Determine concordance between the decision model-recommended therapy (`rec_first_adj`) and the adjunctive vasopressor the patient received during the normal course of care (`first_adj`).

```{r}
fl_aug <- fl_aug |>
  mutate(first_adj_concordance = 
           factor(if_else(first_adj == rec_first_adj, 
                          "concordant", 
                          "discordant"
                          ),
                  levels = c("discordant", "concordant")
                  )
         )

fl_aug |> tabyl(first_adj_concordance) |>
  adorn_totals() |>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |>
  rename(Concordance = first_adj_concordance) |>
  kable(align = c('lcc'),
        caption = "Concordance of Decision Model Recommended and Observed Adjunct"
        ) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

Only 31.8% of patients received the decision model-recommended adjunctive vasopressor (the medication with the highest predicted probability of response) during the standard course of care.

Show the observed incidence of response among concordant and discordant cases.

```{r}
fl_aug |> tabyl(response, first_adj_concordance) |>
  adorn_totals(where = c("row", "col")) |> 
  adorn_percentages(denominator = "col") |>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |>
  adorn_ns(position = "front") |>
  adorn_title(placement = "combined") |>
  rename("Response (row)/Concordance (col)" = `response/first_adj_concordance`) |>
  kable(align = c('lcc'),
        caption = "Observed Response Incidence by Decision Model-Recommendation Concordance"
        ) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

Show data similarly in a contingency table (with interpretation below).

```{r}
Epi::twoby2(fl_aug$first_adj_concordance, fl_aug$response)
```

Adjunctive vasopressor response was observed in 178 of 769 (23.1%) patients receiving discordant vasopressor therapy and 137 of 359 (38.2%) patients receiving concordant vasopressor therapy (difference in percentages 15.0% [95% CI; 9.2%, 20.9%]).

Create a numeric response outcome variable, then determine the association of concordance with adjunctive vasopressor response using logistic regression.

```{r}
fl_aug <- fl_aug |>
  mutate(response_bin = as.integer(response == "Response"))

discord_analysis <- glm(response_bin ~ first_adj_concordance,
                        data = fl_aug, family = binomial(link = "logit")
                        )

tidy(discord_analysis, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(term = sub("^first_adj_concordance", "", term)) |>
  select("Term" = term, "OR" = estimate, 
         "95% CI, Lower" = conf.low, "95% CI, Upper" = conf.high) |>
  kable(align = c('lcccc'),
        caption = "Logistic Regression for Adjunctive Vasopressor Response by Decision Model Concordance",
        digits = 2
        ) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

Decision model-concordant adjunctive vasopressor therapy was associated with 2-fold higher odds of response (OR 2.05 [95% CI; 1.56, 2.69]).

### Subgroup: Concordance by Recommended Vasopressor

To gain further insight into the nature of discordance, show concordance by decision model-recommended first adjunctive vasopressor. 

```{r}
fl_aug |>
  mutate(first_adj_concordance = 
           fct_relevel(first_adj_concordance, "concordant")
         ) |>
  tabyl(first_adj_concordance, rec_first_adj) |>
  adorn_totals(where = c("row", "col")) |> 
  adorn_percentages(denominator = "col")|>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |>
  adorn_ns(position = "front") |>
  adorn_title(placement = "combined") |>
  rename("Concordance/Recommended" = `first_adj_concordance/rec_first_adj`) |>
  kable(align = c('lcc'),
        caption = "Concordance by Decision Model-Recommended First Adjunct"
        ) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE)
```

Next, assess whether the association between concordance and response varies according to the decision model-recommended first adjunct by fitting a logistic regression model with an interaction term between recommended first adjunct and concordance. This addresses the question: "Within each recommended first adjunct, what is the odds ratio for response comparing concordant versus discordant therapy?". Then, formally test for effect modification/interaction ("Does the effect of concordance on response differ across recommended first adjunct groups?").

```{r}
fl_aug <- fl_aug |>
  mutate(first_adj_conc_relevl = 
           fct_relevel(first_adj_concordance, "concordant")
         )

fit <- glm(response_bin ~ rec_first_adj * first_adj_conc_relevl,
           family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = fl_aug
           )

(emm <- emmeans(fit,
                pairwise ~ first_adj_conc_relevl | rec_first_adj,
                type = "response"
                ))

emmeans(fit, pairwise ~ first_adj_conc_relevl | rec_first_adj,
        type = "response"
        )$contrasts |>
  summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))

anova(fit, test = "Chisq")

rm(fit)
```

There was some evidence that the association between concordance and response differed by the decision model-recommended first adjunctive vasopressor, but the evidence for effect modification was not substantial (interaction p = 0.09). Concordant therapy was associated with higher odds of response when phenylephrine was recommended (OR 2.40, 95% CI 1.13 to 4.91), whereas no evidence of an association was observed when vasopressin (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.40 to 2.21) or epinephrine (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.23 to 1.77) was recommended.

#### Subgroup: Recommended vs. Received

In a corollary analysis, further assess the nature of discordance by evaluating response by the recommended adjunct and the received adjunct - beyond just concordant/discordant therapy receipt and rather the specific agents. This will be accomplished by fitting a model with an interaction term between the first adjunct recommended (`rec_first_adj`) and the received first adjunct (`first_adj`). Then, assess within each recommended adjunct subgroup how the response odds compare with the concordant therapy.

```{r sub2-rec-receive}
# Fit model to estimate response probabilities (these estimates are the same 
# as observed because the model is saturated)
fit <- glm(response_bin ~ rec_first_adj * first_adj,
           family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = fl_aug
           )

# Estimated response percentages
prob_tbl <- as.data.frame(
  summary(emmeans(fit, ~ rec_first_adj * first_adj, type = "response"))
  ) |>
  transmute(
    rec_first_adj = as.character(rec_first_adj),
    first_adj = as.character(first_adj),
    response_ci = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f, %.1f)", 100 * prob, 100 * asymp.LCL,
                          100 * asymp.UCL
                          )
    )

# ORs relative to concordant therapy within each recommendation stratum

or_tbl <- map_dfr(
  c("vasopressin", "epinephrine", "phenylephrine"),
  \(ref_lvl) {

    fl_aug |>
      filter(rec_first_adj == ref_lvl) |>
      mutate(first_adj = relevel(factor(first_adj), ref = ref_lvl)) |>
      glm(response_bin ~ first_adj, family = binomial, data = _) |>
      tidy(exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
      filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
      transmute(
        rec_first_adj = ref_lvl,
        first_adj = sub("^first_adj", "", term),
        or_ci = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high))
    }
  )

# Add concordant rows
or_tbl <- bind_rows(
  tibble(rec_first_adj = c("vasopressin", "epinephrine", "phenylephrine"),
         first_adj = c("vasopressin", "epinephrine", "phenylephrine"),
         or_ci = "1.00 (Reference)"),
  or_tbl
  )

# Final table
discord_analysis_sub2 <- prob_tbl |>
  left_join(or_tbl,
            by = c("rec_first_adj", "first_adj")
            ) |>
  mutate(
    rec_first_adj = factor(rec_first_adj,
                           levels = c("vasopressin", "epinephrine",
                                      "phenylephrine"
                                      ),
                           labels = c("Vasopressin", "Epinephrine",
                                      "Phenylephrine"
                                      )
                           ),
    first_adj = factor(first_adj,
                       levels = c("vasopressin", "epinephrine", 
                                  "phenylephrine"
                                  ),
                       labels = c("Vasopressin", "Epinephrine",
                                  "Phenylephrine"
                                  )
                       )
    ) |>
  arrange(rec_first_adj, first_adj) |>
  rename(`Recommended Adjunct` = rec_first_adj,
         `Received Adjunct` = first_adj,
         `Response, % (95% CI)` = response_ci,
         `OR vs Concordant (95% CI)` = or_ci
         )

(discord_analysis_sub2 |>
  kable(align = c('llcc')) |>
  kable_paper(full_width = FALSE))

#rm(fit, prob_tbl, or_tbl)
```

First, when the model recommends vasopressin the rate (percentage) of response is relatively similar (~40%) regardless of which adjunct was administered. When the model recommends epinephrine and the patient receives epinephrine (concordant therapy), the response rate appears slightly lower compared with receipt of another adjunct. The most intriguing finding is when the model recommends phenylephrine - when the patient receives phenylephrine (concordant therapy) response appears substantially higher compared with receipt of another agent.

When compared to concordant therapy, there was no convincing evidence that following the decision model-recommended therapy improved response when vasopressin or epinephrine was recommended (discordant confidence intervals are relatively wide and include 1). However, among patients in whom phenylephrine was recommended, receipt of discordant therapy with vasopressin (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.21-0.91) or epinephrine (OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.12-0.91) was associated with lower odds of response compared with receipt of phenylephrine.
